CUSTOMER REASSIGNMENT PROCESS (NOT YET BUILT). Who submits: GL for within-group, Admin for cross-group. Self-request not allowed. Steps: (1) GL/Admin raises with reason. New table needed: customer_reassignment_requests with request_id, customer_id, requested_by, old_agent_id, new_agent_id, reason, status PENDING/ACKNOWLEDGED/ACCEPTED/APPROVED/REJECTED, timestamps.

BUILD ORDER AGREED. Sequence: (1) DB schema 8 tables. (2) Models. (3) Transactions read-only group scoped. (4) Customers read+edit group scoped. (5) Claims links to transactions. (6) Vendor payments links to claims. (7) Reconciliation links payments to claims. (8) Commission display - MUST wait for hold/release. (9) Reward points depends on commission. LUMP SUM VENDOR PAYMENT DESIGN. Problem: vendor pays lump sum no breakdown cannot identify claims. Admin records: vendor, date, total amount, bank ref IBG/TT, remittance yes/no. No remittance: Stage 3 shows ONE banner card lump sum total, all pending agent claims as checkbox table below, running total in footer hard blocks if exceeds vendor payment. Yes remittance: Stage 1 auto-match. Partial remittance: Stage 2. Sequence enforced - Stage 3 only unlocks after Stage 2 confirmed. Budget bar shows confirmed green + pending amber + blocked red. System NEVER allows allocated_amount to exceed total_amount.

CLAIMS BUSINESS RULES. Commission frozen for ALL agents GL+TL+Introducer simultaneously on claim submission CR-019. Status flow: PENDING to MATCHED to CONFIRMED to PAID. REJECTED and DISPUTED are terminal. If rejected after commission paid: reversal entry created wallet debited commission_hold_log REVERSED. Agent must reconfirm within 3 days of match - no reply reverts to PENDING NOT_VERIFIED. Admin posts to Commission Payment Request Ledger only after agent reconfirms. Cannot process if unmatched CR-021 hard rule. Only Admin discharges unmatched - must upload manual
verification proof. claim_upload_date = when agent uploaded docs. sales_transaction_date = copied from transaction on claim creation.

TRANSACTION DETAIL DRILL DOWN IMPLEMENTATION. Route: /gl/transactions/{policy_id}?from=customer. The from=customer query parameter controls Back link behaviour - if from=customer then Back link goes to customer detail page, otherwise goes to transactions list. TransactionController show() method queries: sales_transactions joined

with customers, products, agents, vendors filtered by policy_id AND agentIds (group scope enforced). Commission breakdown queries commission_transactions joined with agents filtered by policy_id. Claims queries claims table filtered by policy_id with DATEDIFF to calculate days_outstanding. Commission hold status checked per commission row via commission_hold_log table. Customer name in detail page is clickable link to /gl/customers/{customer_id}.

CUSTOMER DETAIL EXPANDABLE TRANSACTIONS. JavaScript toggleDetail() function in show.blade.php handles row expand/collapse. Each transaction row has onclick=toggleDetail(policy_id). Hidden detail row id=detail-{policy_id} toggles display between none and table-row. Arrow indicator id=arrow-{policy_id} switches between down triangle and up triangle. Sticky table header: thead has position:sticky top:0 z-index:1 so header stays visible while scrolling. Max height 380px on transaction table container with overflow-y:auto for scroll. PRODUCT CODE column: shows p.product_code from products table as clickable link (blue), policy_number shown below in grey as sub-label. Product/Vendor column: shows product_name + product_type + vendor_name all in one cell. This was a deliberate design decision - not all products are policies so Policy No header was incorrect and renamed to Product Code.

MYSQL CONNECTION WITHOUT PASSWORD. Discovery during development: XAMPP MySQL root user has NO password when accessed without -p flag. Command that works: mysql -u root generallink -e "SQL;". Command that fails: mysql -u root -p generallink -e "SQL;" (prompts for password which fails). This is XAMPP default configuration. All database queries during development used: mysql -u root generallink -e "DESCRIBE tablename;" format. PHP Laravel connection uses DB_USERNAME=root DB_PASSWORD= (empty) in .env file.

SCREEN LAYOUT DECISIONS AND DESIGN RATIONALE. (1) Transactions page uses inline CSS not Bootstrap classes because dashboard layout uses Tailwind CDN not Bootstrap - mixed approach. Summary cards use CSS grid not Bootstrap grid. (2) Status badges use custom inline background/color pairs not Bootstrap badge classes - allows precise colour control per status. (3) Customer detail uses 280px fixed left column for info panel, right column takes remaining space - better proportion than equal split. (4) Transaction table in customer detail: max-height 380px chosen to show approximately 5-6 rows before scroll needed. (5) Claims section max-height 200px - claims typically fewer than transactions. (6) Summary cards for transactions show 5 metrics in single row: Total, Active, Pending Renewal, Lapsed, Total Premium - these 4 statuses chosen as most business-relevant for GL.

This ensures no context is lost between sessions. Master Spec Word document serves as the permanent record to share with new Claude sessions.

TRANSACTION STATUS TYPES - ALL 7. Sales transaction status enum confirmed from DB: DRAFT (created not submitted), SUBMITTED (submitted for processing), ACTIVE (policy running), PENDING_RENEWAL (expiring soon), RENEWED (successfully renewed), LAPSED (expired not renewed), CANCELLED (cancelled). Badge colour mapping: ACTIVE=green background #d1fae5 text #065f46, SUBMITTED=blue #dbeafe/#1e40af, DRAFT=grey #f3f4f6/#374151, PENDING_RENEWAL=amber #fef3c7/#92400e, RENEWED=cyan #e0f2fe/#075985, LAPSED=red #fee2e2/#991b1b, CANCELLED=dark #f3f4f6/#6b7280. GL Transactions summary cards show: Total, Active, Pending Renewal, Lapsed, Total Premium (5 most business-relevant statuses).

VENDOR PAYMENT RECONCILIATION DASHBOARD - ENTRY POINT. Before drilling into any specific vendor payment, Admin sees the Vendor Payment Reconciliation Dashboard overview. This shows ALL vendors sorted by urgency. Design: (1) Summary bar at top: Critical count (red), Warning count (amber), Cleared count (green), Total RM locked, Total agents waiting. (2) Red alert strip: names longest waiting agent and days. (3) Filter: by status, sort by urgency/amount/days/vendor name, product type. (4) Vendor rows grouped: CRITICAL section (14+ days overdue, red border), WARNING section (in progress, amber border), CLEARED section (all matched, green border). Each vendor row shows vendor name, payment date, amount, bank ref, amount locked with mini progress bar, stage pills (Remittance Matched/Partial Evidence/Last Attempt), agents waiting with longest name and days, vendor cooperation score (Good/Moderate/Poor/None), action buttons (Resolve Now, Contact Vendor, View Dispute). Title of matching screen is Vendor Payment Reconciliation - [Vendor Name] not just vendor name alone.

PRODUCT CODE vs POLICY NUMBER RENAME. User challenge: column header said POLICY NO but not all products are policies - some are PA, Fire, Motor etc. Decision: rename column to PRODUCT CODE (from products.product_code field). Display format: product_code shown as clickable blue link to transaction detail. policy_number shown below in grey as secondary reference. Rationale: product_code is the primary business identifier that works for ALL product types. policy_number is insurance-specific terminology not applicable to all products. This rename applies to: GL Customer Detail transactions table, GL Transactions list table header. All future modules should use product_code as primary reference not policy_number.

SCROLLABLE TRANSACTION TABLE DESIGN. User requirement: transactions should display in row format, detail as expandable columns, max 10 visible rows with scroll bar. Implementation: table container has max-height:380px and overflow-y:auto for vertical scroll bar. Sticky header with position:sticky top:0 z-index:1 so column headers stay visible while scrolling. Each row is compact - all info in one line. Click row expands detail below as extra table row spanning all columns. Arrow indicator shows direction. Claims section separate scrollable box below transactions with max-height:200px. Same expandable pattern agreed for claims section (same method for claims as transactions).

PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND DELIVERY NOTES. Key feedback from user during development session: (1) Always give full directory path with every file delivery - not just filename. (2) Always deliver files one by one - user standard instruction, never deliver multiple files in single message. (3) Show download button for every file - do not ask user to copy-paste code. (4) Be proactive as system analyst - do not just do exactly what is asked, think ahead about dependencies, data integrity, business impact. (5) Boss was questioning progress - need to show visible working modules quickly. (6) Running out of time - prioritise what is visible to boss first. (7) Not productive to keep debugging login issues - should have fixed root cause properly first time. (8) Claude should behave as intelligent AI system analyst not just a code generator.

CLAIMS MODULE DESIGN - NOT JUST POLICIES CLARIFICATION. User repeatedly corrected that the system is not just for insurance policies. Products include Motor, Personal Accident, Fire, Other. Claims can be raised against any product type not just insurance policies. Therefore: (1) claim_reference not policy_number used as primary identifier. (2) Column header Product Code not Policy No. (3) claim_upload_date = date agent uploaded claim documents. (4) sales_transaction_date = date of original sale transaction copied into claims table. (5) Vendor side dates: sales_transaction_date (when sale was made) and vendor_payment_date (when vendor paid us). (6) Agent side dates: sales_transaction_date (same reference) and claim_upload_date (when agent uploaded documents). Both dates shown on matching screen cards with different colour chips for easy comparison.

(1) claims: claim_id, claim_reference, policy_id FK, customer_id FK, agent_id FK, vendor_id FK, product_id FK, claim_amount, approved_amount, sales_transaction_date, claim_upload_date, status (PENDING/MATCHED/CONFIRMED/PAID/REJECTED/DISPUTED), commission_held (auto=1 on submit), commission_released_at, rejection_reason, notes. (2) claim_documents: document_id, claim_id FK, document_type (POLICE_REPORT/RECEIPT/IC/MEDICAL_REPORT/REPAIR_ESTIMATE/OTHER), file_name, file_path, file_size bytes, uploaded_by FK. (3) vendor_payments: payment_id, payment_reference, vendor_id FK, payment_date, bank_reference, total_amount, allocated_amount, unallocated_amount (computed), remittance_provided, remittance_file_path, matching_stage, status, flag_count, recorded_by FK. (4) vendor_payment_allocations: allocation_id, payment_id FK, claim_id FK, allocated_amount, matching_stage, match_method (AUTO/MANUAL/LUMP_SUM), vendor_ref_provided,

verified_by FK, verified_at, agent_confirmed, agent_confirmed_at, agent_confirmation_deadline (3 days), status (PENDING/AGENT_NOTIFIED/CONFIRMED/REVERSED/NOT_VERIFIED), reversal_reason. (5) commission_hold_log: hold_id, claim_id FK, commission_txn_id FK, agent_id FK, role_at_transaction, held_amount, hold_reason (CLAIM_PENDING/VENDOR_UNMATCHED/AGENT_NOT_CONFIRMED), held_at, released_at, released_by FK, status (HELD/RELEASED/REVERSED). (6) claim_matching_log: log_id, payment_id FK, claim_id FK, stage, action, performed_by FK - IMMUTABLE. (7) financial_audit_log: audit_id, event_type, entity_type, entity_id, amount_before, amount_after, metadata JSON, performed_by FK, ip_address - APPEND ONLY, never updated or deleted. (8) vendor_performance: perf_id, vendor_id FK, total_payments, remittance_provided_count, auto_match_rate, avg_days_to_pay, flag_count, dispute_count, cooperation_score (GOOD/MODERATE/POOR/NONE), termination_warned, termination_warned_at.

8 LARAVEL MODELS CREATED. Claim.php - auto-generates claim_reference, auto-sets commission_held=1 on create, releaseCommission() helper method, scopes: active(), pending(), held(). ClaimDocument.php - fileSizeFormatted accessor. VendorPayment.php - auto-generates payment_reference, canAllocate() checks budget, isFullyAllocated(), flagVendor() auto-triggers dispute at 3 flags, auto-updates VendorPerformance. VendorPaymentAllocation.php - auto-sets agent_confirmation_deadline 3 days, on CONFIRMED status auto-releases commission hold, updates vendor payment allocated_amount, marks claim as PAID, updates CommissionHoldLog. CommissionHoldLog.php - placeHoldForClaim() static helper freezes all agents in chain. ClaimMatchingLog.php - immutable log. FinancialAuditLog.php - record() static helper, prevents updates and deletes via model events. VendorPerformance.php - updateCooperationScore() recalculates GOOD/MODERATE/POOR/NONE, auto-sends termination warning at 3 flags.

VENDOR PAYMENT RECONCILIATION DESIGN - 3-STAGE SCREEN. Stage 1 Remittance Matched: vendor gave full remittance with product code/ref, system auto-matches, shows 2-column card view (LEFT=Vendor remittance, RIGHT=Agent claim). Each card shows: Sales Ref No, Customer name, Product name, Product type badge (Motor=blue, PA=green, Fire=amber, Other=grey), Coverage dates, Claim amount, Sales Transaction Date (blue chip), Vendor Payment Date / Claim Upload Date (amber chip). Verified Match checkbox in middle column. Stage 2 Partial Evidence: vendor gave some info but no ref no. Missing fields shown in red italic. Admin matches by customer name, product, amount, date. Stage 3 Last Attempt: no vendor info, single lump sum. Admin ticks from agent claim list table. System blocks selection if exceeds vendor payment total. Progress strip shows current stage and locked stages. Vendor Reconciliation Dashboard: shows ALL vendors sorted by urgency - Critical (red, 14+ days), Warning (amber, in progress), Cleared (green). Each vendor row shows: amount locked + mini progress bar, stage status pills, agents waiting + longest wait days, vendor cooperation score. Record new vendor payment button. Summary bar: critical count, warning count, cleared count, total RM locked, total agents waiting.

LIVE BALANCE TRACKER DESIGN. Always visible at top of matching screen. Shows: (1) Vendor paid in - total received RM in blue. (2) Unlocked and released - RM in green with commission processing label. (3) Pending this stage - RM in amber with stage name. (4) Still locked - RM in red across all stages. (5) If you confirm now - shows exactly how much releases and to how many agents instantly - makes business impact clear to admin. Master progress bar: green=released %, amber=pending %, red=locked %. ORGANIZATIONAL HIERARCHY, PROMOTION, DEMOTION & BREAKAWAY BUSINESS RULES DOCUMENTED (BACKLOG - DESIGN ONLY, NOT YET BUILT). This entry captures the business logic discussed and agreed for the agent hierarchy / commission engine, to be implemented in a future session. AGENT_CODE CONVENTION CHANGE: existing role-prefixed codes (GL-00001, TL-00001, I-00001/I-00002) are being replaced with a single role-neutral prefix "A-" (e.g. A-00001) for ALL agents regardless of role - agent_code is a permanent identifier assigned once at registration and NEVER changes, even when the agent is promoted or demoted through GL/TL/Introducer roles; the CURRENT role is read live from agents.role and shown via the existing colour-coded role badge, never inferred from the code prefix. The existing 4 seed agents (GL-00001 Chris Yap, TL-00001 Ahmad Razif, I-00001 Siti Nurhaliza, I-00002 Rajan Pillai) are to be renumbered A-00001 through A-00004 in created_at order as part of this change. Sequence numbering is per-prefix (each entity type - Agent "A-", Customer "C-", Transaction, Claim, Vendor Payment, Admin - has its own independent counter), generated via a single hardcoded CodeGeneratorService/constants mapping so the convention is consistent system-wide. NEW FIELD origin_group_id (immutable): set once at first registration to record which GL's group the agent originally joined; this value is NEVER overwritten by any later promotion/demotion/breakaway, providing permanent traceability of "which GL originally brought this person into the business" for historical reporting and any origin-based override calculations. AUTOMATIC PROMOTION RULE (Introducer/TL -> GL): trigger is purely structural - whenever an agent has 3 or more directly-downline agents holding role=TEAM_LEADER, that agent is AUTOMATICALLY promoted to GROUP_LEADER by the system with no admin approval required ("policy-driven"). No income/production target is required for this promotion step. On promotion: (1) a new group_id is created for the promoted agent; (2) the promoted agent's ENTIRE recursive downline subtree (everyone whose parent_id chain traces back to them, however many levels deep, i.e. "agents recruited by their team or themselves") is reassigned to the new group_id and has hierarchy_path rebuilt; (3) promoted agent's parent_id is set to NULL; (4) role_history logs old_role/new_role/effective_date; (5) origin_group_id is preserved unchanged. CRITICAL EXCEPTION - "WHAT MOVES" ON PROMOTION: if any member of the promoted agent's downline had THEMSELVES previously broken away to form their own GL group (i.e. they are no longer in the promoted agent's subtree because they already left), that branch is NOT pulled back in - only the CURRENT subtree moves. THE FORMER UPLINE IS NOT PENALISED: e.g. if Introducer Rajan (under TL Ahmad, under GL Chris) is promoted to GL because Rajan's own recruits produced 3 TLs, only RAJAN's subtree moves to Rajan's new group - Ahmad's structure, role, parent_id and remaining downline are completely UNCHANGED; Ahmad simply stops earning commission on Rajan's (and Rajan's downline's) future sales, but keeps all historical earnings and his position - Ahmad remains free to be promoted to GL later via his own merits. BREAKAWAY BONUS RULE (separate from the structural promotion trigger above): triggered when the newly-promoted (or an existing) agent's group hits a defined EARNING/PRODUCTION TARGET (a different metric from the "3 TLs" headcount rule) - this is a ONE-TIME bonus payout (not an ongoing override), paid via the rule "walk up the parent_id chain starting from the promoted agent's IMMEDIATE FORMER PARENT, and pay the first agent found whose role = GROUP_LEADER". Worked example: if Rajan breaks away (hits earning target) while his immediate former parent Ahmad is CURRENTLY a GL, the bonus goes to Ahmad; if Ahmad is NOT (yet) a GL at that moment, the bonus skips Ahmad and goes to the next GL up the chain (Chris Yap). This walk-up-to-first-active-GL function (findNearestActiveGL) is a single reusable routine used for both the breakaway bonus AND the demotion re-parenting rule below. AUTOMATIC DEMOTION RULE (GL -> TL): unlike promotion, demotion's TRIGGER may originate from an admin action or policy condition (to be defined), but once triggered the ENTIRE CASCADE IS FULLY AUTOMATIC / SYSTEM-DECIDED with no further admin judgment calls, governed by these rules: (1) RULE - A TEAM LEADER'S PARENT IS ALWAYS A GROUP LEADER, NEVER ANOTHER TL: the demoted agent's new parent_id is resolved via findNearestActiveGL(their former position) - e.g. if Ahmad currently holds GL role, demoted-Rajan reports to Ahmad; otherwise Rajan reports to Chris Yap; if Chris Yap is inactive, falls to Chris Yap's designated beneficiary (requires new field beneficiary_agent_id on agents table - a named successor who inherits a GL's role/responsibilities if that GL becomes inactive). (2) RULE - WHAT THE DEMOTED AGENT BRINGS BACK: only their OWN downline that did NOT themselves separately become GL during the demoted agent's time as GL - any former downline member who broke away and became GL on their own merit stays independent and is NOT pulled back into the demotion; this is the exact mirror of the promotion "what moves" rule. (3) RULE - COMMISSION ENTITLEMENT AFTER DEMOTION: the demoted agent (now TL) does NOT retain GL-tier or TL-tier earning power over their former downline; they earn ONLY the Introducer-tier "overriding" commission on agents they personally introduced (recursively), at the percentage defined in commission_structures for their CURRENT role (TL) - role_at_transaction remains the authoritative field for all historical commission_transactions, unaffected by the demotion. (4) DECIDED 03 Jul 2026 (was: OPEN QUESTION): disposition of the demoted agent's now-empty/shrunk group_id — RESOLVED: mark the groups row is_active = false (soft-delete pattern), NEVER hard-delete it. Rationale: identical principle to the Introducer-deletion decision made the same day — historical sales_transactions and commission_transactions permanently reference this group_id, and physically deleting the row would break or orphan that financial/audit trail. The group_id record itself is cheap to retain forever; the risk of deleting it is not. This mirrors soft-delete via status/is_deleted already used elsewhere in the schema (agents.status, agents.is_deleted). DATA ISOLATION / MULTI-TENANCY CONFIRMED: an entirely separate, unrelated organisation (a different GL or set of GLs with their own group_id(s), e.g. "Group B" with a few thousand agents onboarded via the same bulk Excel import mechanism as Section 58's migration tooling) is FULLY ISOLATED from Chris Yap's group via the existing DataScopeService group_id-based scoping (per v9.0) - enforced at the query/controller level (not merely hidden in the UI), so Chris Yap can never access Group B's records and vice versa; only Admin (the 3-admin layer, also documented as backlog) sits above all groups with cross-group visibility for oversight, customer reassignment, and financial reconciliation. Large-volume imports (few thousand agents) should run in chunked batches with a "dry-run validation" mode (checks duplicate IC numbers, missing parent references, invalid emails etc. WITHOUT writing to the database) before committing, plus a credential-generation/export step for bulk new user accounts. ALL ITEMS IN THIS ENTRY ARE DESIGN/POLICY DECISIONS ONLY - implementation (schema migrations for origin_group_id/beneficiary_agent_id/role_history/breakaway_bonus_log, the CodeGeneratorService, the PromoteAgentService/DemoteAgentService cascade logic, and the Excel bulk-import tool from Section 58) remains to be built in a future session. RECRUITMENT DEPTH LOCK RULE DOCUMENTED (BACKLOG - DESIGN ONLY, NOT YET BUILT) + INTRODUCER DASHBOARD BUGFIXES (BUILT). RECRUITMENT DEPTH LOCK RULE - clarifies and extends the v59 promotion thresholds: an Introducer CAN recruit new Introducers as direct downline (e.g. Siti Nurhaliza, an Introducer, recruits Lim Wei Ming and Nurul Aina as her direct downline Introducers) - BUT those newly-recruited Introducers (Lim Wei Ming, Nurul Aina) CANNOT themselves recruit any further downline AS LONG AS THEIR RECRUITER (Siti) REMAINS AN INTRODUCER. The SAME "3" THRESHOLD APPLIES AT EVERY LEVEL, symmetrically: (a) an Introducer with 3 OR MORE DIRECT INTRODUCER RECRUITS auto-promotes to TEAM_LEADER (mirroring the v59 rule "3 direct TL recruits -> auto-promote to GROUP_LEADER" one level up - both are instances of the same general "3 direct recruits at role X -> promote to role X+1" policy). (b) ONLY ONCE THE RECRUITER IS PROMOTED does their downline's recruitment capability UNLOCK - e.g. once Siti reaches 3 direct Introducer recruits and auto-promotes to Team Leader, Lim Wei Ming and Nurul Aina (now operating under a Team Leader, a structurally valid "level 2" position) become free to recruit their OWN downline Introducers for the first time. This prevents a newly-recruited Introducer's branch from "out-leveling" their own still-Introducer recruiter, and ties recruitment permission directly to the upline's current promotion status - this is the intended purpose of the existing agents.recruitable_tier_depth column (currently defaults to 0 for all agents) and agents.recruitment_blocked flag: recruitment_blocked should be TRUE for any Introducer whose direct parent_id agent is ALSO role=INTRODUCER (i.e. two consecutive Introducer levels with no TL/GL between them blocks the lower one from recruiting), and should flip to FALSE automatically the moment the parent agent is promoted to TEAM_LEADER (cascading recalculation, same trigger pipeline as the v59 promotion cascade). WORKED EXAMPLE FROM TODAY'S TEST DATA: Siti Nurhaliza (I-00001, Introducer, under TL Ahmad Razif) recruited 2 new Introducers today - Lim Wei Ming (I-00003) and Nurul Aina (I-00004), both with parent_id=Siti, 0 transactions, status=ACTIVE, login credentials limweiming@generallink.my / nurulaina@generallink.my (password123). Per the rule above, both I-00003 and I-00004 should currently have recruitment_blocked=TRUE (Siti is still an Introducer, only 2/3 toward her own promotion threshold) - once Siti recruits ONE MORE direct Introducer (reaching 3) she auto-promotes to Team Leader, at which point I-00003 and I-00004 unlock and may begin recruiting their own downline. NOTED GAP: there is currently NO UI for an Introducer to view or manage their own direct-Introducer downline (the Introducer dashboard, per the v58 standardisation, is scoped entirely to "my own sales/commission/rewards" with no equivalent of TL's /tl/introducers page) - a future "My Recruits" page for Introducers (mirroring /tl/introducers, scoped to the Introducer's own direct downline) is needed once the recruitment-depth rules above are implemented, so agents like Siti can see Lim Wei Ming and Nurul Aina listed under her. *** CRITICAL / FOUNDATIONAL RULE - READ BEFORE IMPLEMENTING ANY COMMISSION OR PROMOTION LOGIC ***

THE UNIVERSAL RECURSIVE OVERRIDE RULE (BACKLOG - DESIGN ONLY, NOT YET BUILT, BUT MANDATORY DESIGN CONSTRAINT FOR ALL FUTURE COMMISSION-ENGINE WORK). This entry generalises and SUPERSEDES any temptation to special-case the Siti / Lim Wei Ming example from v60 - there is NO special-case logic anywhere in this system for "who overrides whom"; there is exactly ONE rule, applied identically and recursively to EVERY adjacent upline-downline PAIR in the hierarchy, at every level, for every transaction: "Whether agent A (upline) earns an ongoing commission override on agent B's (downline) sales depends ENTIRELY on (i) agent B's group_id currently matching a group that agent A's CURRENT role entitles them to earn from (i.e. B is currently 'inside' A's group as far as the org chart is concerned), AND (ii) agent A's and agent B's CURRENT roles at the time of B's transaction, looked up in commission_structures via the standard role_at_transaction mechanism." WORKED EXAMPLE CHAIN (illustrative, not exhaustive): Siti (Introducer) recruits Lim Wei Ming (Introducer) -> no override relationship yet beyond the standard Introducer-tier the immediate upline TL/GL already earns. Siti is promoted to TEAM_LEADER (3 direct Introducer recruits, v60 rule) -> Siti now earns the standard TL-tier override on Lim Wei Ming's sales (Lim Wei Ming is in Siti's TL downline). Siti is later promoted to GROUP_LEADER (3 direct TL recruits, v59 rule) -> Siti now earns the GL-tier override on Lim Wei Ming's sales PROVIDED Lim Wei Ming is STILL a TL inside Siti's new group (group_id continuity) - this is JUST THE NORMAL GL-OVERRIDE MECHANISM, nothing new is required. If Lim Wei Ming is THEN ALSO promoted to GROUP_LEADER (breaks away with his own subtree, v59 rule) -> Siti STOPS earning ongoing override from Lim Wei Ming (and his subtree) from that point forward - Lim Wei Ming is now a peer GL, not inside Siti's group - EXCEPT for the one-time breakaway bonus per v59 (paid to Siti if she is GL at that exact moment). If Lim Wei Ming is LATER DEMOTED back to TEAM_LEADER (v59 demotion rule: TL's parent must always be the nearest active GL, found via findNearestActiveGL) -> Lim Wei Ming re-parents to WHICHEVER GL IS NEAREST/ACTIVE AT THAT MOMENT - this MAY be Siti again (if she is still GL and is the nearest), in which case the override relationship AUTOMATICALLY RESUMES with no special code, OR it may be a DIFFERENT GL if circumstances have changed (e.g. Siti herself was demoted, or a closer GL now exists) - the rule does not "remember" Siti as Lim Wei Ming's original sponsor for override purposes; it ONLY looks at CURRENT group_id + CURRENT roles. THE SAME RULE APPLIES ONE LEVEL DOWN, RECURSIVELY, WITHOUT LIMIT: if Lim Wei Ming (as TL or GL) has his OWN downline member, and THAT member is promoted/demoted/breaks away, the IDENTICAL rule (group_id continuity + current roles + role_at_transaction lookup) determines whether Lim Wei Ming continues earning from that member - completely independent of, and using the exact same logic as, the Siti/Lim-Wei-Ming pair one level up. IMPLEMENTATION IMPLICATION: as long as (a) group_id reassignment is correctly cascaded to the ENTIRE moving subtree on every promotion/demotion/breakaway event (per v59's PromoteAgentService/DemoteAgentService), and (b) every commission_transactions row correctly records role_at_transaction + the agent's group_id-at-that-time, THEN the existing commission_structures role-based lookup ALREADY PRODUCES THE CORRECT OVERRIDE AMOUNTS FOR EVERY PAIR AT EVERY LEVEL AUTOMATICALLY - no additional "sponsor override", "originator override", or pair-specific tables/logic are needed or should be built. Any future developer proposing a special-case override table for a specific named relationship (e.g. "Siti's override on Lim Wei Ming specifically") should be pointed back to this entry - it is very likely unnecessary and indicates the group_id cascade or role_at_transaction lookup is not being relied upon correctly. RECRUITMENT-LOCK ESCAPE MECHANISM DOCUMENTED (BACKLOG - DESIGN ONLY, NOT YET BUILT). Resolves the v60 concern "what if a recruiter (Siti) never reaches the 3-recruit promotion threshold - are her blocked downline (Lim Wei Ming, Nurul Aina) stuck forever?" Confirmed: NO automatic time-based INACTIVE status change based on an agent's own sales activity (an earlier graduated DORMANT/INACTIVE proposal based on sales inactivity was REJECTED in favour of the simpler, more targeted mechanism below). THE ESCAPE MECHANISM - triggered at the moment a blocked Introducer (e.g. Lim Wei Ming) attempts to recruit a new sub-Introducer; the system checks TWO conditions, EITHER of which unlocks: CONDITION A (admin 4-eye): the blocked Introducer's direct recruiter (Siti) has been set to status=INACTIVE via the existing 3-admin 4-eye / dual-approval process (2 of 3 admins must both confirm the status change, consistent with the bank-signatory dual-authorization pattern documented earlier this session) - this is a discretionary admin action, not automatic, typically prompted by a stagnation review. CONDITION B (time-based, automatic): the system finds the RECRUITMENT DATE OF THE RECRUITER'S 2ND DIRECT INTRODUCER RECRUIT (for Siti, this is whichever of Lim Wei Ming/Nurul Aina was recruited second - the "2nd recruit date" marks the point Siti reached 2-of-3 toward her own promotion threshold) and checks whether (today - that_2nd_recruit_date) > inactive_period_duration, a NEW configurable value stored in a master settings table (admin-configurable, system-wide, in days). If EITHER condition A or B is true, recruitment is allowed. BATCH UNLOCK, NOT PER-INDIVIDUAL: when either condition is satisfied for Siti, ALL of Siti's direct recruits who were recruitment_blocked (BOTH Lim Wei Ming AND Nurul Aina) unlock TOGETHER as a single batch at that moment - the check and unlock are evaluated against the RECRUITER'S (Siti's) situation, not independently per blocked-downline-individual. FULLY RECURSIVE / SYMMETRIC AT EVERY LEVEL: once unlocked, if Lim Wei Ming recruits his own sub-Introducers (Person X, Person Y) and Lim Wei Ming HIMSELF later becomes "stuck" (2-of-3, exceeding inactive_period_duration measured from HIS 2nd recruit's date, OR Lim Wei Ming is set INACTIVE via the same 4-eye process), THEN Person X and Person Y unlock together via the IDENTICAL mechanism, checked relative to Lim Wei Ming's situation - exactly as Lim Wei Ming/Nurul Aina were checked relative to Siti's. Each "stuck-at-2-of-3" Introducer generates their own independent timer (from their own 2nd recruit's date) and their own independent INACTIVE-eligibility under the 4-eye process; resolving it unlocks their entire direct-recruit cohort as a batch - the unlock for any individual is NOT permanent/global in isolation, it is a consequence of THEIR DIRECT RECRUITER's situation being resolved. NEW FIELDS/TABLES REQUIRED (not yet built): settings.inactive_period_duration (integer, days, admin-configurable); a query/index to efficiently find "the Nth direct-Introducer-recruit's created_at" per agent (likely via ROW_NUMBER() over agents partitioned by parent_id ordered by created_at, or a dedicated recruitment_order column); the existing 3-admin 4-eye approval_requests mechanism (documented earlier this session for bank-signatory actions) extended to cover agent status changes to INACTIVE for this purpose. ANY business - restaurant, grocery, furniture, florist, hardware, clinic, hotel, insurance, etc.

GeneralLink AFFILIATE AGENTS - agents buy from vendors, not external customers

GL % + TL % + Introducer % = Total rebate. Always 100% distributed.

✅ Data scope enforced at CONTROLLER level - not just UI

✅ Introducer cannot access any other agent's data - 403 Forbidden
✅ All unauthorized access attempts logged in audit_logs table

✅ TL with 50 Introducers - queries 50 records only
✅ Database indexes on group_id and parent_id - lightning fast
✅ Cache per group - GL cache invalidated only when his group data changes
✅ Dashboard loads in < 1 second even with millions of records

8. Commission Engine - CR-001 to CR-018
Rule
Description
Commission flows along parent_id chain ONLY - never sideways
Commission based on role AT TIME OF TRANSACTION
System walks UP parent_id until first qualified role found
Demoted agent's portion goes UP to next qualified role in same direct line
GL receives all unallocated TL portions below him in direct line
TL-B NEVER receives commission from sales by Introducer under TL-A
INACTIVE agent commission goes to registered beneficiary
No beneficiary = commission to Suspended Ledger - held permanently
Admin must upload approved PDF to release from Suspended Ledger
Company management must approve every adjustment entry
Every commission transaction logged permanently - never deleted
Total distribution ALWAYS equals 100% of vendor rebate
Only ONE TL in direct chain receives TL commission
Only ONE GL in direct chain receives GL commission
parent_id never changes - only role field changes
System auto-demotes when direct count falls below threshold
System auto-promotes when direct count meets threshold
GL can demote all the way to Introducer if loses qualifications

18. Commission Hold & Release Policy
⚠ CRITICAL: Commission hold and release is directly tied to the vendor payment reconciliation process. No commission is released until vendor payment is confirmed through all applicable stages.
18.1 New Commission Rules (CR-019 to CR-026)
Rule
Description
When a claim is submitted against a transaction, commission for ALL agents in the chain (GL + TL + Introducer) is FROZEN immediately and automatically.
Commission is released ONLY after vendor payment is received AND confirmed through the 3-stage matching process (Remittance Matched, Partial Evidence, Last Attempt).
System CANNOT release commission if vendor payment total has not been received. No exceptions. Cannot pay more than vendor paid in.
Commission hold applies to ALL roles in the transaction chain simultaneously. GL commission held, TL commission held, Introducer commission held - all at the same time.
Commission release is automatic upon Admin confirming the vendor payment match. System releases all held commissions for that transaction instantly to GL, TL and Introducer wallets.

If claim is rejected or disputed after commission was already paid out, a commission reversal entry is created. The reversal is logged in commission_hold_log with status REVERSED. Agent wallet is debited accordingly.

If vendor is uncooperative and claim cannot be matched after all 3 stages, Admin may manually discharge the claim by direct verification with vendor and agent. This requires Admin to upload proof of manual verification. Commission released ONLY after upload and approval.
Every commission hold and release event is logged permanently in commission_hold_log and financial_audit_log. These logs are immutable - never deleted or updated. Full audit trail maintained forever.
18.2 Commission Hold Flow - Step by Step
Step
Action
System Behaviour
Agent submits claim
claims.commission_held = 1 auto-set. commission_hold_log records GL + TL + Introducer hold entries. All notified immediately.
Admin records vendor payment
vendor_payments record created. matching_stage = REMITTANCE_MATCHED. Admin alerted to begin matching.
Stage 1 - Remittance Matched
System auto-matches by product code/ref. Matched claims move to confirmed. Unmatched move to Stage 2.
Stage 2 - Partial Evidence
Admin matches manually using partial vendor info. 2-column card view. Unresolved move to Stage 3.
Stage 3 - Last Attempt
Admin manually allocates from agent claim list. System blocks if total exceeds vendor payment. Still unresolved = Formal Dispute triggered.
Agent reconfirms matched claim
Agent receives notification. Must reconfirm within 3 days. No reply = reverts to Pending with NOT_VERIFIED flag.
Admin posts to commission release queue
Admin confirms final posting. System releases commission to GL, TL, Introducer wallets simultaneously. All notified immediately. commission_hold_log status = RELEASED.

19.9 Future Backlog Items & Security Posture - Logged 12 Jun 2026 21:13
1. Database Backup & Restore (Admin Module) - NOT BUILT
Proposed as a future "System Maintenance" section under Admin: trigger a mysqldump export for download, and restore from an uploaded .sql file. Not in scope for current sessions - added to backlog.
2. Mobile Responsiveness - NOT CATERED FOR

All pages built to date (Commission, Profile, Admin Dashboard, GL Dashboard, Network drill-down) use desktop-only fixed-position layouts: Prev/Next buttons at hardcoded left:276px / right:16px, height:calc(100vh-Npx) full-screen sections, and 4-column metric grids. On mobile screens the sidebar does not collapse correctly with these fixed positions, and grids would be too cramped to use. A dedicated responsive pass (media queries, sidebar collapse behaviour, vertical stacking of cards) is required before the system can be used on mobile devices. Added to backlog - not in scope for current sessions.
3. View-Source / Front-End Code Protection - ACCEPTED AS-IS, NO ACTION NEEDED

HTML/CSS/JS delivered to the browser can always be viewed via Inspect/View Source - this is fundamental to how browsers work and is true of every website including banks. This is NOT a security concern for this system: all business logic (commission formulas, database queries, role permission checks) runs server-side in Laravel/PHP and is never sent to the browser; sensitive fields (NRIC, bank account) are already encrypted/masked in the Profile module; and RoleMiddleware enforces authorization server-side regardless of what is visible client-side. DECISION: no front-end obfuscation (right-click disable, DevTools blocking, JS minification for "protection") will be pursued, as these provide false security and add maintenance burden. Current server-side-only approach for sensitive logic is the accepted and final security posture for this system.

The previous Bootstrap-style page (3 summary cards + separate filter bar + 15-row table, all on a scrollable page) was identified as "ugly/fat" and redesigned to a single non-scrolling screen. REMOVED: the 3-card summary header entirely - the "Total Customers" and "Showing" cards were duplicating the same number (both showed $customers->total()), and "States Covered" was low-value on this screen; all three removed.

CRITICAL DATA-VOLUME DECISION: the page no longer auto-loads the full customer list on first visit. In a real environment this table could hold millions of rows and an unfiltered SELECT would hang the page. Controller now checks $hasQuery (true if search, state, agent_role, sort_by or page is present in the request); if false, no database query for the customer list runs at all and the table body shows an empty-state row "Use the filters above to search for customers". ADMIN CUSTOMER SEARCH (NOT BUILT - design discussion only): when Admin views customers across all groups, a single "Owned By" filter is not enough to locate where a customer sits in the hierarchy. Recommended design: three cascading dropdowns - Group Leader, Team Leader, Introducer - each including an explicit "All" option. Selecting a Group Leader (e.g. "Chris Yap") with Team Leader = All and Introducer = All returns every customer owned by any Team Leader or Introducer under that Group Leader. Each result row should display the full ownership chain (Introducer name -> Team Leader name -> Group Leader name), not just the immediate owner, resolved via two levels of agents.parent_id. Default sort: agent_code ascending. This requires the cascading dropdowns to populate dynamically (JS) based on the parent selection.

CUSTOMER REASSIGNMENT (Admin-only, NOT BUILT): re-raised during this session in the context of a customer wanting to switch away from a poorly-performing or suspended/terminated agent. Confirmed this should be Admin-only (not self-service by GL/agent) and must keep a full audit trail (who changed it, when, old value, new value, reason). This aligns with and extends the existing customer_reassignment_requests design already logged at v23.0 (request/acknowledge/accept/approve workflow, past commissions stay with original owner, future sales go to new owner). To be scoped and built in a future session.

21.4 Business Rules Confirmed (Permanent)

FILTERING MANDATORY: Every list page must show empty state with filter prompt until user applies at least one filter. No default load of all records. In live production any list can have 100,000+ records - default load = system crash. This rule applies to ALL list pages without exception forever.

STANDARD FILTER SET (agent/introducer lists): Search by name/agent code, State/Location, Date Joined (from/to), Status (Active/Inactive/Terminated), Top Sales Amount, Top Commission Earned, Number of Transactions, Recruitment Blocked (Yes/No).

DOWNLINE EDIT RIGHTS: GL can edit his TLs' and Introducers' contact details (phone, email, bank name, address only). TL can edit his Introducers' contact details. Introducer can edit his recruits' contact details. Nobody can edit Full Name, NRIC, bank account number through the system.

PROMOTION TRACKING: Every role change (INTRODUCER → TEAM_LEADER → GROUP_LEADER) must be logged to audit_logs with action='ROLE_CHANGE', before_value=old role JSON, after_value=new role JSON, agent_id=who made the change. Network Tree pages will show a promotions counter per agent row querying audit_logs. GL/TL/Introducer can see how many of their downlines were promoted. Admin can see all promotions across all GLs.

DRILL-DOWN RULE (universal): Admin → all GLs → each GL’s TLs → each TL’s Introducers → each Introducer’s recruits. GL → his TLs → Introducers → recruits. TL → his Introducers → recruits. Introducer → his recruits. Individual profile visible at every level. Once an agent breaks away to GL, they leave the original group and are no longer visible in the former GL's tree.

Promotion Date = date agent's role changed from TL to GROUP_LEADER - system automatic, NO Admin involvement

26. GL Creation Methods and Network Visibility Rules - 26 Jun 2026
26.1 CRITICAL Terminology
ALWAYS use these terms - never use Breakaway GL:

26.2 GL Creation Methods
There are exactly 2 ways a GL can be created:
Method A - Auto-Promotion (Internal Network)
A TL whose own recruits produce 3 direct TLs is automatically promoted to GL by the system
They came from within the existing network - recruited by an existing GL, TL or Introducer
On promotion: new group_id created, entire subtree moves, parent_id set to NULL - fully automatic, NO Admin involvement
origin_group_id = the group they originated from (the GL whose group they were in before promotion)
Can be demoted back to TL - promotion/demotion history recorded in role_history table
Method B - Excel Batch Import (External Organization)
An entire external organization affiliates with GeneralLink - e.g. Police Cooperasi, a company group, any organization not recruited by existing GL/TL/Introducer
Admin imports their data via Excel batch import - the ENTIRE group comes in together as one unit
The imported GL is a founding GL - not recruited by anyone in the system
origin_group_id = NULL - they are completely independent from day one
RULE: Admin CANNOT create a GL manually one by one - ONLY via Excel batch import of an external organization
The Excel data comes from another portal or external organization's own records
Future methods (C, D, etc.) may be added as business grows
26.3 Network Visibility Rules - CRITICAL
These rules are permanent and must be enforced at controller level via DataScopeService:

Cannot See

ALL GLs regardless of method - Method A, B, C, D etc. Full visibility across all groups and all data

A GL can ONLY see Promoted GLs that originated FROM their own group
A GL is completely blind to GLs from other groups regardless of creation method
The No. of Promoted GL count in Box 2 only counts GLs promoted FROM THIS GL's group - not all GLs in the system
This visibility rule applies to ALL screens - dashboard, network, transactions, commissions, customers

27. Admin Dashboard Issues, Fixes and Lessons Learned — 26 Jun 2026
27.1 What Went Wrong — Root Cause Analysis
Issue 1: Admin Blade File Corrupted by Multiple Python String Replacements
Root cause:
Multiple sessions of Python string replace operations on the same file caused duplicate HTML blocks
BOX 4, BOX 5, BOX 6 appeared 2-3 times in the same file
The file grew from 499 lines to 700+ lines with duplicate content
Each replace operation appended content instead of replacing in-place
Lesson learned:
NEVER use multiple string replace operations on the same blade file across different sessions
Always verify box count with regex after any file modification: re.findall(r'BOX d+:', content)
If duplicates found - STOP and rebuild from clean backup
Always keep a clean backup of every blade file before modifying
Issue 2: Box Layout Looked Wrong After More Agents Were Added
Root cause:
Admin dashboard was originally designed for ~50 agents and few transactions
After seeding 215 agents and 1637 transactions, boxes 1/2/3 overflow because more data
Tried to fix by reducing font sizes multiple times - made things worse
The correct fix was to increase grid row heights only
Lesson learned:
When data volume increases, fix grid row heights FIRST before touching font sizes
Grid row heights: grid-template-rows:1.8fr 2.2fr 95px gives enough space for current data
Do NOT reduce font sizes below: ct=7px, row-lbl=9px, row-val=10px, perf=8px
Always test with realistic data volume before declaring done
Issue 3: GL Dashboard Metrics Calling Admin Routes
Root cause:
GL dashboard blade was copied from admin blade but admin route names were not updated
metricsUrl still pointed to admin.dashboard.metrics instead of gl.dashboard.metrics
drilldown links pointed to /admin/dashboard/drilldown
chart-drilldown blade hardcoded route('admin.dashboard') for backUrl
Lesson learned:
When copying admin blade to GL - search and replace ALL admin route references
Key routes to check: metricsUrl, drilldown base URL, chart-drilldown backUrl, perfDrillUrl
The chart-drilldown.blade.php is SHARED between admin and GL - use auth('agent')->user()->role check
Code: $isGL = auth('agent')->check() and auth('agent')->user()->role === GROUP_LEADER
Issue 4: Drilldown Vendor/Product Queries Not Scoped to GL Group
Root cause:
GL DashboardController chartDrilldown() and drilldown() methods were missing agentIds filter
Vendor and product queries returned data from ALL agents not just GL group
This caused amount mismatch between Box 4/5 on dashboard vs View All drilldown screen
Lesson learned:
Every query in GL controller MUST use whereIn('agent_id', agentIds) or whereIn('st.agent_id', agentIds)
agentIds must be fetched at the start of EVERY controller method - not just index()
Add getAgentIds() private method to GL controller and call it at start of every public method
Issue 5: Agent Code Appearing as Stray Character in Top Performers Box
Root cause:
perf-sub div was showing agent_code which for GL is '1', '1-1', '2' - appeared as lone number
This confused the user who saw '1' below Chris Yap name
Lesson learned:
For GL/TL/Intro performer cards - show full_name and role badge only
agent_code is useful for admin view but confusing for GL view
Remove perf-sub div from GL dashboard performer cards
Issue 6: Pie Chart Colors Conflicting with Bar Chart Colors
Root cause:
Bar chart uses: Sales=Blue #1565C0, Earning=Green #1B5E20, %=Orange #D97706
Pie chart was also using same blue/green/orange colors causing confusion
User could not distinguish vendor slices from sales/earning/% meaning
Lesson learned:
Pie chart for vendor/product must use DIFFERENT colors from bar chart
Approved pie colors: Vendor 1=Light Blue #90CAF9, Vendor 2=Light Yellow #FFF176, Vendor 3=Pink #F48FB1
These colors are clearly distinct from Sales Blue, Earning Green, % Orange
Issue 7: GL Network Screen - Team Total vs TL Own Sales Confusion
Root cause:
GL network screen was showing TL own sales only - not team total
When drilling to Introducer screen, TL Own + Intros = different from GL network total
Caused confusion because numbers did not tally
Lesson learned:
GL network screen MUST show team total per TL = TL own sales + all Introducer sales under that TL
Use separate query to calculate team total for each TL - not just TL agent_id sales
Introducer drill down header must show: TL Own Sales + Intros = Team Total
Team Total must equal exactly what GL sees for that TL on network screen

28. Agent Promotion Rules (Session 01 Jul 2026)
28.1 Promotion Thresholds
Introducer to Team Leader: When an Introducer reaches 3 or more direct sub-Introducers, they are automatically promoted to Team Leader (TEAM_LEADER role).

Team Leader to Group Leader: When a Team Leader has 3 or more directly promoted Team Leaders under them, they are automatically promoted to Group Leader (GROUP_LEADER role) and form their own independent group.
28.2 Visibility Rules

A Team Leader CAN see all Promoted TLs in their dashboard Box 1 (Promoted TL tab) and Box 2 (Promoted TL count). This is necessary so the TL knows how many more Promoted TLs are needed to reach GL promotion.
A Team Leader CANNOT see a Promoted TL only when that Promoted TL has been elevated to Group Leader and breaks away to form their own independent group.
A Promoted TL (still under their TL) CANNOT see their parent TL full team data. They can only see their own sub-team downward.
Once a Promoted TL becomes a Group Leader, they form their own independent group and CANNOT see their former TL team data.
28.3 Example - Wendy Koh

Wendy Koh (code 1-4-1) was originally an Introducer under Tan Boon Hwa (TL, code 1-4). After recruiting 4 sub-Introducers (Faridah Yusof, Tan Wei Jian, Saravanan Muthu, Lim Hui Min), she was promoted to Team Leader on 01 Jul 2026.
Tan Boon Hwa can see Wendy Koh as a Promoted TL in his dashboard. He needs 2 more Promoted TLs to be eligible for GL promotion.
Wendy Koh logs in as TEAM_LEADER role and sees only her own team. She cannot see Tan Boon Hwa full team data.

33. Admin Network Screens — 02 Jul 2026
33.1 Design Philosophy — Filter First

All Admin network screens now follow filter-first pattern — no records are loaded until the user applies a filter or clicks Show All. This is critical for live environment with potentially 300+ GLs, 250,000+ TLs and 5,000,000+ Introducers. Loading all records would hang the system.
33.2 Admin Network GL List (/admin/network)

Filter bar: Show All | GL Name typeahead | Status | Joined From | Joined To | Go | Clear. GL Name uses AJAX typeahead — type any letter, matching GL names appear in dropdown. Results show: # | GL Name | Code | TLs count | Intros count | Sales MTD | Status | Joined. Top 3 GLs show medals. Click any GL row goes to TL list screen.
33.3 Admin Network All TLs (/admin/network/all-tls)

Filter bar: Show All | TL Name typeahead | GL dropdown | Status | Joined From | Joined To | Go | Clear. TL typeahead is scoped — when GL is selected, typeahead only returns TLs under that GL. Results: # | TL Name | Code | GL Name | Intros count | Sales MTD | Earning Income MTD | Status | Joined.
33.4 Admin Network By-GL (/admin/network/gl/{id})
Shows TL list under a specific GL. Filter-first. TL Name typeahead scoped to that GL only. Breadcrumb: All GLs > GL Name > Team Leaders. Prev button goes back to All GLs.
33.5 Admin Network By-TL (/admin/network/gl/{glId}/tl/{tlId})

Shows Intro list under a specific TL. Filter-first. Intro Name typeahead scoped to that TL only. Breadcrumb: All GLs > GL Name > TL Name > Introducers. Prev button goes back to GL TL list. table-layout:auto prevents name truncation.
33.6 Admin Network All Intros (/admin/network/all-intros)

Most complex filter screen. Filter bar: Show All | Intro Name typeahead | GL dropdown | Show (Direct Only / All incl TLs) | TL dropdown (visible when GL selected) | Status | Joined From | Joined To | Go | Clear.
Direct Only mode: shows only intros whose parent_id = selected GL agent_id (Chris Yap has 10 direct intros: Vincent Ho 1-9, Raymond Goh 1-13, etc.)
All (incl TLs) mode: shows intros whose parent_id is GL or any TL under that GL (Chris Yap has 33 total).
TL dropdown: when specific TL selected, shows only direct intros under that TL (Tan Boon Hwa = 3 intros).
When GL selected: TL column hidden. When GL + TL selected: both columns hidden. No redundant repeated data.
Sort order: LENGTH(agent_code), agent_code for natural numeric ordering.
33.7 AJAX Typeahead Endpoint
URL: /admin/network/ajax/typeahead?q={query}&mode={gl|tl|intro}&scope={parent_agent_id}

Mode gl: returns GROUP_LEADER agents matching query. Mode tl: returns TEAM_LEADER agents, scoped to parent GL if scope provided. Mode intro: returns INTRODUCER agents, scoped to parent TL if scope provided.

37. DEVELOPER HANDOVER DOCUMENT — GeneralLink Project
Version: v100 | Date: 02 July 2026 | Prepared for: New Chat Developer
37.0 MANDATORY STANDING PROJECT RULES (Effective 20 Jul 2026 onward)
These rules apply to every future session on GeneralLink, without exception, until Chris says otherwise. Any new chat continuing this project must read this section first, before touching any code.
37.0.1 Screen Design Rules — Mandatory on Every Screen
— No scrolling in any direction (up, down, left, or right). Every screen must fit and display fully within one view.
— Navigation between related screens/steps must use Previous / Next buttons only. No jump-navigation or hidden shortcuts that could disorient the user.
— No truncated labels or truncated record values anywhere. If content is too long for the space, the layout must be redesigned (wrap, resize, reflow) — never cut off with "...".
— One standard font family and size used across all screens. No ad hoc per-screen font choices.
— One standard colour scheme used across all screens. No ad hoc per-screen colours.
37.0.2 Working Method Rules

— Chris does not write or edit code. The assistant (Claude, acting as coworker) makes all code changes directly — creating, editing, or removing PHP/Blade files itself. Chris is never asked to open a file and make an edit himself.
— Every new or changed file is saved directly into the connected project folder (C:\xampp\htdocs\generallink) as part of the work, automatically — never left only in a temporary/scratch location.

— Chris only ever runs already-prepared Command Prompt (cmd) instructions — e.g. php artisan migrate. No multi-click GUI deployment steps. Commands are given one at a time, in order, exactly as Chris should type them.
37.0.3 Session Continuity Rules

— Whenever Chris signals a session is ending ("continue later", "continue tomorrow", "I need a break", or similar), the assistant must, before ending: write up everything done in that session as a dated activity/development log entry, and append it into this Master Spec document, incrementing the version number and date in the filename (e.g. master-spec-v113-200726.docx → master-spec-v114-210726.docx).

— When Chris returns and says "continue", the assistant must first read the latest Master Spec file, then save a fresh dated snapshot copy of it into C:\xampp\htdocs\version log\ with a new filename, before starting any new work — so every session's starting state is preserved as its own permanent snapshot.
37.0.4 Backup Rule — Adjusted From Chris's Original Request, See Note
Chris's original request (20 Jul 2026): copy the entire C:\xampp folder to Google Drive every 2–3 days at 1am, automatically.

— Adjustment agreed and explained to Chris the same session: copying the whole C:\xampp folder is unnecessary (it includes Apache/MySQL/PHP program files, not just project data) and copying live MySQL database files directly while the server is running risks a corrupted, unusable backup.

— Correct approach instead: (1) the project code folder (C:\xampp\htdocs\generallink) is backed up continuously via the Google Drive desktop app's own folder sync — always up to date, no schedule needed, no AI step required. (2) The database is backed up via a proper mysqldump export to a timestamped .sql file, run on a schedule via Windows Task Scheduler (the same mechanism already set up for the Laravel scheduler), saved into a folder that Google Drive is watching.
— Status: recommendation given to Chris 20 Jul 2026; the mysqldump script + Task Scheduler entry itself is not yet built — pending Chris's go-ahead.
37.0.5 Data / Query Safety Rules (Effective 2 Aug 2026)

— NEVER auto-display records on page load. Every screen that lists or aggregates data (reports, ledgers, transaction lists, agent rosters, etc.) must start empty with a Select/Filter prompt, and must only run its database query AFTER Chris (or the logged-in agent) actively picks a filter and presses Go — no exceptions, regardless of how few rows the table currently holds.

— This applies especially to any query that aggregates or joins against a transaction-type table (commission_transactions, sales_transactions, override_ledger_entries, withdrawal_requests, etc.) — these are the tables most likely to grow into millions of rows over time, and an unfiltered aggregate over them is exactly the kind of query that can hang or crash the whole system.

— Trigger: raised by Chris on 2 Aug 2026 after the newly-built Earning Income Ledger roster loaded all 469 agents (with Debit/Credit totals computed across all of them) on first page load, with no filter applied yet. Fixed same session: the roster query is now skipped entirely (not just hidden in the view) until a real filter/team-member selection is submitted.

GeneralLink Digital Affiliate Ecosystem is a Laravel PHP web application for managing a multi-level insurance affiliate network. The system supports 4 user roles: Admin, Group Leader (GL), Team Leader (TL), and Introducer. Each role has its own dashboard, network drill-down screens, transaction views, and Excel exports.

37.7 Critical Developer Rules — READ BEFORE CODING

RULE 1 — STEP BY STEP DEPLOYMENT: The developer (user) is a beginner. Always give files ONE AT A TIME. Each file must be downloaded and deployed before moving to the next. Never give multiple files at once without confirmation.
RULE 2 — ALWAYS PROVIDE DOWNLOAD: After every code change, always use present_files tool to give the user a downloadable file. Never just show code in chat — always make it downloadable.
RULE 3 — CONFIRM BEFORE NEXT FILE: After each file deployment, wait for user to say "next" or "done" before proceeding to next file.
RULE 4 — NO REFACTORING: Do NOT refactor to common blade architecture. Risk too high. Each role has its own separate blade files. Keep it this way until all roles are fully tested.
RULE 5 — READ FILES BEFORE EDITING: Always upload and read the current live file before making changes. Never edit from memory.
RULE 6 — TEST IN TINKER FIRST: Before writing controller code, verify the query works in tinker. Never guess at data.
RULE 7 — MONTH/YEAR: All queries must respect the selected month/year from dashboard. Never use now()->month as default without passing it through navigation.
RULE 8 — SORT ORDER: Always use orderByRaw(LENGTH(agent_code), agent_code) for natural numeric sort. Never use orderBy(agent_code) alone.
RULE 9 — EARNING INCOME: The word Commission must be replaced with Earning Income on ALL screens. Audit every screen you touch.
RULE 10 — FILTER FIRST: All network drill-down screens must be filter-first (no records until filter applied). Critical for live environment with millions of agents.

37.9b Business Decisions Made 03 Jul 2026 (Master File Maintenance planning)

DECISION 1 - Introducer deletion: Admin can NEVER hard-delete an Introducer (or any agent). "Delete" in Introducer Maintenance means changing status to TERMINATED only. Rationale: agent_code and upline (parent_id) are permanent per registration rules; the agent may have downlines and sales_transactions/commission_transactions history that would be orphaned or lose audit trail if the row were removed. Default rule (revisable): if an Introducer still has active sub-Introducers under them, block the status change with an error rather than silently orphaning the downline.

DECISION 2 - New Introducer creation must follow the SAME registration + email verification process as the public /register page (Method B), whether initiated by Admin (Master File Maintenance), or by an existing GL/TL/Introducer inviting a new recruit. There is no separate/simpler "direct insert" path for Admin - this keeps agent_code generation, upline assignment, and identity verification consistent regardless of who initiates it.

DECISION 4 - Group_id disposition on GL demotion (resolves Section 59 open question): mark groups.is_active = false, never hard-delete. Same rationale as Decision 1 - protects historical financial/audit trail.

DECISION 5 - Re-promotion group_id: if a demoted GL (e.g. Amy Tan, TL->GL->TL) is promoted to GL again later, she gets a BRAND NEW group_id each time - her old (now inactive) group_id is never reinstated/reused. Rationale: her actual membership will be different each time (new recruits since the demotion), so reusing the old ID would misrepresent history; matches the spec's literal wording "a new group_id is created" with no special case for re-promotion.

DECISION 6 - Displaced downline reunification: when a GL is demoted, her subordinate TLs (and their downlines) that get reassigned to the nearest active GL above her (e.g. Chris Yap) are marked as "displaced, not permanent" (requires a new field, e.g. displaced_from_agent_id, on the agents table). If she is later promoted to GL again, the system automatically reunites this displaced downline back to her new group_id - EXCEPT any former downline member who became a GL themselves in the interim, who stays independent per the existing "what moves" exception rule (Section 59). Her own direct Introducers were never displaced in the first place (a TL is allowed direct Introducers under demotion), so this rule only concerns the subordinate-TL layer and their downlines. IMPORTANT OPERATIONAL NOTE (raised by user): promotions/demotions can happen within minutes of each other under real registration volume, so this displaced-downline tracking and reunification logic must be built with the same DB transaction + row-locking safeguards as evaluateRankChange() to avoid race conditions or an agent being left in an inconsistent parent/group state mid-cascade.

SEQUENCE NUMBER column: every list/table must show a sequence number (#) as the very first column. NO DUPLICATE TITLES: the browser topbar already shows the page title (via @section('page-title')) — do not repeat the same heading again as a large h2 on the page body. One title only.

LOCKED / NON-EDITABLE FIELD STYLING: light blue background (#E0F7FA) with light blue border (#B2EBF2) and NORMAL BLACK TEXT — never grey background with grey text (too washed out, hard to read). 37.13.3 Business Decisions Made This Session

Email edit on an EXISTING record follows the same standard as public registration: changing email requires the new address to be verified via a link before it takes effect. agents.email is never touched until confirmed — the new value sits in pending_email/pending_email_token in the meantime. Confirmed after a full impact study: tier structure, sales transactions, commissions, and audit trail are all unaffected by an email change since they key off agent_id, never email — the only real impact is login access.

Reason codes are NOT hardcoded in PHP — they live in a real database table (reason_codes: category, code, description, is_active), pre-seeded with a starting list (Termination: Voluntary Exit, Non-Performance, Policy Violation, Customer Complaint, Fraudulent Activity, Deceased, Other. Delete: Duplicate Entry, Data Entry Error, Registration Abandoned, Test Record, Other). Admin should eventually be able to add/edit these via a Reason Code Maintenance screen — agreed but NOT YET BUILT (see 37.13.5).

Notification broadcast rule — New Registration and Promotion: notify the direct sponsor, every Introducer in that Group, every Team Leader in that Group, the Group Leader, and Admin — both email and in-app bell. Reasoning: visibility into group activity keeps everyone motivated, and a new person may already know others in the group. Demotion is narrower: only the PREVIOUS leader (the one demoted) plus Admin — no group-wide broadcast.
Notification trigger timing: fired only AFTER real email verification succeeds, never at initial form submission — a mistyped or abandoned registration must never falsely notify anyone.

QR referral system: every agent has a permanent qr_code_token (column already existed in schema, unused until this session). The QR code encodes a URL like /register?ref={token} — deliberately using this private token, NOT the real agent_code, so a public QR image can never be used to guess/enumerate nearby hierarchy codes. QR images are generated live client-side (qrcode.js) from the stored token — never stored as an image file, since the same token always regenerates the identical image.

Registration sponsor selection now offers 3 methods, in this priority order: (A) scan or upload the sponsor's QR code image (decoded client-side via jsQR, then looked up by token — also auto-selects the correct Upline Type), (B) wildcard search by name or partial code with a live pick-list dropdown, (C) fully automatic if the person arrives via a scanned QR link (?ref=TOKEN already in the URL on page load).

NRIC and Bank Account Number are shown as the FULL decrypted value on the Admin-facing Introducer Edit screen — this was Admin's explicit, informed decision after a security trade-off discussion (the alternative, masking to last 4 digits, was offered and declined).

Bank Account Number is editable by Admin on the Introducer Maintenance Edit screen, even though an Introducer cannot edit their own bank account number directly through their own Profile page — this matches the existing GL/TL Profile Edit convention ("Bank account number locked, Admin only").

Profile pictures: stored on local server disk for now (storage/app/public/profile-pictures), with only the file PATH saved in agent_profiles.photo_path — never the raw image data in the database. Plan to migrate to AWS S3 or DigitalOcean Spaces later if/when scale requires it (Laravel's storage abstraction makes this a low-effort future change). Filenames are Laravel's own randomly-generated names — deliberately NEVER the person's IC number (privacy/security risk if leaked via URL/logs) and never their full name (not unique, causes URL-encoding issues).
Admin's own profile gets the photo upload feature but explicitly does NOT get a QR referral code, since Admin does not personally recruit prospects the way Introducer/TL/GL do.

Introducer Maintenance "Add" reuses the exact same register.blade.php form and AuthController::register()/verifyEmail() logic as public registration — reconfirmed this session, no separate/simpler direct-add form exists or should exist, per Decision 2 (37.9b).

Status Update (Active / Inactive / Terminated) requires a reason code (mandatory only when setting Terminated) plus optional free-text notes, and is BLOCKED from setting Terminated if the Introducer still has active sub-Introducers under them (Decision 1) — Admin must reassign or terminate the downline first.

Delete rule (reconfirmed): true hard-delete is only permitted if the record was never email-verified (a genuine wrong/duplicate entry with nothing depending on it). Once verified, "Delete" can only ever mean setting status to Terminated, subject to the same downline-block rule above. The actual Delete screen itself was NOT YET BUILT this session — see 37.13.5.
37.13.4 Root Cause Bug Found and Fixed — Introducer Maintenance search returning 0 results

Symptom: searching Introducer Maintenance by any field appeared to work for Full Name, but always returned 0 records the moment the Status or Recruitment Blocked dropdowns were left on their blank default option, even when real matching data existed and had already been proven to exist via direct tinker queries.

Root cause: Laravel's built-in ConvertEmptyStringsToNull middleware converts every blank submitted form field to PHP null, not an empty string. The controller's Status and Recruitment Blocked filter checks used a fragile `!== ''` string comparison instead of Laravel's `filled()` helper. Since `null !== ''` evaluates to true in PHP, the code wrongly concluded the field had been filled in, and silently added `WHERE agents.status IS NULL` (and a similar false condition for recruitment_blocked) to every single search query — breaking all searches regardless of what the user actually typed. The Full Name filter worked correctly the whole time because it used the safer `$request->filled()` check, which correctly treats null as blank.
Fix: replaced the fragile comparisons with `$request->filled('status')` and `$request->filled('recruitment_blocked')` consistently, matching the pattern already used correctly for the other fields.

This took a multi-hour debugging session to isolate. Ruled out first, in order: browser caching, Apache not truly restarting, PHP OPcache (confirmed not even installed on this server), and stray/duplicate controller files (a real prior issue in this project, but not the cause here) — confirmed via a raw closure-based bypass route proving the query logic itself was correct outside the controller, and a literal SQL comment marker proving the exact controller file in question WAS what was executing, before the true root cause (the middleware's null-conversion behavior) was found by directly printing the raw PHP variable values at runtime.

37.20 Session — 12 Jul 2026 — Group Isolation Security Architecture

Following the login-level security fixes above, a further, broader requirement was raised: Special Privilege Group data (dashboards, KPI boxes, network tree, search) must be fully isolated from other groups everywhere in the system, not just at login — and different Special Privilege Groups must never see each other's data anywhere.
37.20.1 Chosen Architecture — Global Scope
Chris specifically suggested a single centralized rule (checking the logged-in user's own group once) rather than auditing/patching many individual screens — this shaped the final design.

— GroupIsolationScope.php (new): an Eloquent Global Scope registered once on the Agent model, automatically applied to every Agent:: query anywhere in the app, with zero changes needed to individual screens
— Standard groups completely unaffected — the scope does nothing for anyone not belonging to a genuine Special Privilege Group
— Special Privilege Group members strictly confined to their own group's data only
— Admin given a choice based on HOW they logged in — via a specific group's branded page isolates Admin to that group's data for the session; via the standard page gives the full combined view
— Logout correctly returns each type of user to the appropriate page
37.20.2 Honest, Flagged Limitation

The Global Scope only protects code written using Eloquent's Agent:: syntax — it cannot retroactively protect any existing raw DB::table('agents')-> queries. A full audit of all cached files was performed: the most critical file, MasterFileController.php (all Introducer/TL/GL Add/Search/View/Edit/Status-Change screens, 41 queries), plus ApprovalController, ApprovalService, FinanceWithdrawalController, NotificationService, and WalletController were all confirmed to use Agent:: exclusively — fully protected automatically. Remaining raw-query files (self-service profile controllers, BatchRegistrationService, HierarchyService, SpecialGroupController) were assessed as lower risk and flagged as a separate follow-up.
37.20.3 Two Bugs Found and Fixed During Deployment

— Recursion bug: the scope initially called Auth::user(), which itself triggers an Agent:: query, creating infinite recursion during Laravel's own internal auth resolution and causing a redirect loop. Fixed using Auth::id() (session-only, no query) plus an explicit withoutGlobalScope() bypass for the viewer's own record lookup.

— Self-exclusion bug: when isolating Admin to a specific group, the filter also incorrectly excluded Admin's own account record, since Admin's own group_label_id is NULL. Fixed by explicitly allowing the viewer to always see their own record regardless of the isolation filter.
