38. Session - 2-3 Aug 2026 - AI Assistant Carolyn: Persona, Real Voice, Guided Navigation & Per-Agent Cost Distribution

Covers the introduction of the embedded AI Assistant across the whole app, its evolution into a real branded persona with genuine voice synthesis, a first phase of AI-guided on-screen navigation, and a full redesign of who pays for AI usage as the platform scales.
38.1 AI Assistant Introduced - Carolyn Persona, Avatar & Browser Voice

- New app/Services/AiAssistantService.php + app/Http/Controllers/Shared/AiAssistantController.php: a role-aware conversational assistant powered by the Anthropic Claude API (model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001), reusing the existing HTTP/error-handling pattern from ClaudeDocumentExtractionService/ClaudeTranslationService. One endpoint serves both the guest (login page) and every authenticated screen - mode (guest/agent) is detected from whether an agent session exists, never declared by the caller.

- Persona named Carolyn - a cheerful, warm, young Malaysian-English-sounding AI persona, explicitly honest that she is an AI, never claiming to be human. System prompt enforces strict role-based access (never discusses data/actions outside the logged-in role's scope, per the same rules as the rest of the app), gives only general non-guaranteed business-growth suggestions, never states or implies specific earnings, and defers legal/financial/tax questions to a licensed professional or Admin/Compliance.
- log_ticket tool - Carolyn can log a complaint/bug/question as a ticket (new ai_assistant_tickets table, migration 2026_08_03_000001) for a human team member to follow up on, notifying all Admins.

- resources/views/partials/ai-assistant-widget.blade.php - a floating chat bubble + panel, included on the login page and every authenticated dashboard layout, later extended to every page in the registration/verification pipeline (register, security-phrase, set-password, verification-success, verify-email, verify-pending) after it was found missing from all of them.
- Avatar: originally a hand-drawn SVG rabbit, replaced with a user-uploaded illustrated photo (public/images/carolyn-avatar.png).
- Browser-based speaker mode (Web Speech API, SpeechSynthesisUtterance) added, ON by default, auto-speaking Carolyn's greeting when the panel is first opened.

- Hands-free continuous Voice Mode added (click the mic once, speak, get a spoken reply, mic resumes automatically) using the browser's free SpeechRecognition/webkitSpeechRecognition API, lang set to en-GB (found to transcribe Malaysian English more accurately than en-US).
38.2 Real Voice - ElevenLabs Integration

- Browser TTS judged scary/wrong-accent by Chris; new app/Services/ElevenLabsService.php + app/Http/Controllers/Shared/AiVoiceController.php integrate ElevenLabs (Chris's own paid account) for a genuinely natural female voice (Jessica), with automatic silent fallback to the free browser voice if ElevenLabs is ever unreachable, unconfigured, or out of quota.
- public/voice-test.html - a standalone tool for browsing ElevenLabs' voice catalogue, previewing samples, and saving a choice.

- /ai-assistant/voices, /ai-assistant/speak (now superseded, see 38.6), /ai-assistant/set-default-voice - initially placed in routes/api.php (no CSRF) after a 419 CSRF error was traced to voice-test.html having no session/CSRF token at all.

- FIX: saved voice choice was originally localStorage-only (didn't survive different origins/browsers) - moved to server-side storage/app/carolyn-voice.json. FIX: auto-pick-default logic could land on a male voice when Chris's preferred name list didn't match his account's actual voices - added a prefer any female-labelled voice tier. FIX: voice-test.html's Try my line preview button was silently overwriting the saved selection - decoupled preview from save.
38.3 Voice-Consistency & Mic RCA (Round 1) - Instrumentation

- Per Chris's explicit request, a formal Root Cause Analysis was performed (not immediate code changes) for two reported issues: the spoken voice randomly changing, and the microphone silently dying after 1-2 turns.

- Added: per-request correlation IDs threaded through every related log line; an explicit client-side state machine (idle|listening|processing|speaking) with transition logging; a monotonic turn-ID counter that discards stale/out-of-order async responses; a pin on first success rule - the ElevenLabs voice_id actually resolved on a conversation's first successful call is pinned (via a new X-Voice-Id response header) and sent explicitly on every later call in that browser tab, so a setting change elsewhere can never swap the voice mid-conversation; mic-reinitialization safeguards - a 4-second start-watchdog that force-aborts and retries (max 2) a SpeechRecognition instance that never fires onstart, plus short delays before recreating the recognizer after natural silence or after Carolyn finishes speaking.

- Root cause actually found (via log evidence, not the mic-lifecycle hypotheses): ElevenLabs' monthly quota was exhausted (confirmed via repeated HTTP 401 quota_exceeded responses). The pinning/resolution logic itself was verified to be 100% consistent (identical resolved_voice_id on every logged call) - the different voice users heard was the automatic, working-as-designed fallback to the browser's own voice, not a bug.

- FOLLOW-UP FIX: the browser fallback voice itself was found to have two real bugs of its own - Chrome sometimes hadn't finished asynchronously loading its voice list on the very first utterance (silently producing a random OS-default voice), and the picked voice was never actually persisted anywhere. Fixed by properly waiting for the voiceschanged event (with a 400ms timeout safety net) and pinning the resolved fallback voice by name in localStorage, reused across every page and every future visit on that device/browser.

Fixed by shrinking the left logo panel (48%->32% width, logo max-width 320px->250px) and shifting the sign-in form left (padding adjustment), rather than touching the chat widget itself.
38.5 AI Guided Navigation - Design & Pilot Implementation

- New capability, deliberately separate from the conversational assistant: Carolyn can actively walk a user through a real multi-step task on-screen - open the right page, highlight the right field, explain it, wait for the human to actually do it, then continue. Full design written to docs/ai-guided-navigation-design.md before any code, covering architecture, the action vocabulary, backend/frontend changes, security, and testing strategy.

- HARD RULE (Chris's explicit decision, confirmed 2 Aug 2026): the AI never clicks, submits, or changes anything itself, under any circumstances - every action is highlight-and-explain only; the human performs every click and keystroke. There is no auto-click exception, not even for harmless Next buttons.

- New App\Services\NavigationRegistryService - loads config/ai_navigation/*.php manifests (plain declarative data: pages, elements, authored workflows), validates every referenced route actually exists, filters by role, and is the single re-validation gate a proposed action must pass before ever reaching the browser.

- New App\Services\AiGuidanceService - Phase 1 scope: walks only AUTHORED workflows step-by-step (deterministic array lookup, no live model call per step); ad-hoc AI-improvised planning for goals with no authored workflow is explicitly deferred to a later phase.
- New App\Http\Controllers\Shared\AiGuidanceController + routes (web.php, session-bearing): POST /ai-assistant/guide/start, POST /ai-assistant/guide/next.

38.9 Cost Research - Voice Provider Pricing Comparison (advisory, no code)

- Confirmed Chris's personal Gemini Pro consumer subscription does NOT include any API access - Google keeps the consumer chat subscription and the developer API (Google AI Studio / Google Cloud, its own separate billing) completely separate.

- Pricing found: ElevenLabs - free tier 10,000 characters/month; paid tiers from $5/month (Starter) up to $22/month for 100,000 characters (Creator), scaling to $990/month (Business); roughly $150-220 per million characters at typical tiers. Google Cloud Text-to-Speech - 1 million characters/month free for its higher-quality Neural2/Studio voices (4 million/month free for its standard-tier voices), then approximately $16 per million characters after that (or $4/million on the standard tier) - roughly 10-15x cheaper than ElevenLabs per character at volume, generally considered a notch below ElevenLabs in voice naturalness.

Fixed by adding 'Accept': 'application/json' to every write-assist fetch call (Notice Board's own script plus the shared carolyn-write-helper-script.blade.php), so real error messages (CSRF/validation/etc.) now surface instead of a one-size-fits-all failure.

39.7 Vendor Rebate Scheme - Design Proposal (NOT YET BUILT)

- Chris raised that the existing Offer Request flow (vendor/agent submits promo text, Admin approves, posts to Notice Board) has no formal vendor sign-off with evidence, no audience targeting, and no tracking at all of actual rebate redemptions or fraud controls once real money is involved. Per Chris's explicit instruction, NO CODE was written - a full design proposal was produced instead, as a standalone document: vendor-rebate-scheme-design-v2.docx (saved in the GeneralLink root folder, not yet approved).

- Proposed process: vendor submits scheme -> Admin reviews/adjusts final terms -> Admin sends terms back to vendor -> vendor formally confirms in the Vendor Portal by re-entering their password against the exact frozen final terms (plus an optional signed-document upload for higher-value schemes) -> only then does it go live, targeted to a specific audience (reusing Broadcast Campaigns' existing audience_type/role/group_label targeting model instead of Notice Board's current broadcast-to-everyone) -> every redemption afterward is written to a new Rebate Redemption Ledger (same pattern as the existing Earning Income Ledger) so GeneralLink remains the system of record - and can produce sales history, per-agent rebate earnings, and a leaderboard - even when the vendor pays the rebate directly rather than money moving through GeneralLink.

- Fraud control proposed as layered defence, not one control (explicitly framed this way since no single control stops genuine cashier/affiliate collusion): take the approval decision away from the cashier entirely; a three-way match principle (borrowed from accounting fraud control) requiring independent agreement between the affiliate's own declaration, GeneralLink's own issuance/redemption log, and the vendor's own reconciliation report; reuse of the existing Risk Review Queue (fraud_review_flags table) for pattern-based detection (unusual request frequency/amounts); a per-agent/per-period rebate cap to bound damage; and vendor contractual liability for their own staff's fraud.

- Refined further per Chris's own counter-proposal (credited to him, not treated as a rubber-stamp): rather than a separate native mobile app (rejected as an unnecessarily large build - app-store submission/review, a second codebase, ongoing dual maintenance), the same affiliate-initiated-declaration idea is delivered as a guided flow inside the existing GeneralLink web app (reachable via a menu item and through Carolyn, works on any phone browser, no install), reusing the AI document-reading already built for Document Credit to check bill-photo legibility and auto-extract amount/date/reference number.

- Timing/SOP resolved into two explicit steps after Chris pointed out a claim can genuinely be submitted days after the spending occurred: Step 1 (time-critical, at the premises before paying) - affiliate requests a short-lived Intent Code (QR + short alphanumeric, e.g. RDC-482913) and shows it to the cashier, who simply hand-writes it onto the receipt's existing remarks/reference line - no scanner or POS integration assumed, so it works at any vendor regardless of till sophistication. Step 2 (not time-critical, any time within a claim window such as 30 days) - the affiliate photographs that same receipt and submits the claim whenever convenient, since the evidence is already fixed on paper from Step 1. A claim with no matching code, or a mismatched one, is never auto-rejected - it is still accepted but routed to Admin for manual review instead of being fast-tracked, so an honest mistake doesn't feel like an accusation.

- OUTSTANDING as of end of this session: Chris asked for further deep research specifically on reducing affiliate friction/tedium in this flow (avoiding a perception of the process being too tedious, and avoiding dissatisfaction complaints) before he gives final confirmation to build anything. No implementation (migrations, controllers, screens) has begun - this entire item remains DESIGN ONLY pending that follow-up and Chris's explicit go-ahead.

50.1 STANDING RULE - Multi-Language Support is Now MANDATORY for All Future Development (per Chris, 18 Aug 2026)

- Every new screen, program, or feature built into GeneralLink from 18 Aug 2026 onward MUST support English / Bahasa Malaysia / Chinese display from day one - this is not an optional nice-to-have or a later-phase polish item.
- This is now the same non-negotiable tier of rule as 'no scroll' and 'Prev/Next navigation only, no jump screens' - every future build must comply automatically, without being asked each time.

- Concrete requirement: all static text (labels, headers, buttons, placeholders, table headers, empty-state messages, tooltips, validation messages) must be written using Laravel's __('namespace.key') helper referencing lang/en/, lang/zh/, and lang/ms/ files - never hardcoded English strings directly in a Blade view.

- Reason (Chris's own words, paraphrased): failing to do this creates real user complaints, because real users depend on this - Chinese-speaking CBE/Tao group members, Bahasa-speaking PVATM/ORG agents, and any future non-English-first user.

- This applies to DSG, ORG, and CBE equally - it is NOT a CBE-only requirement. The language-switching mechanism and eligibility are role-based (every agent regardless of group type can switch), not group-specific, so every screen every role can reach must comply.

56. GLADE Public Model — Membership Categories & Annual Platform Fee (27 Aug 2026) — NEW BUSINESS MODEL, DICTATED VERBATIM BY CHRIS, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED

- Chris dictated this in full and explicitly asked it be written into the master spec immediately, mid-discussion of Box 6’s “new subscription member” approval item. Six categories for the GLADE Public Model, based on the number of covered users, with a transparent Annual Platform Fee structure. ALL figures below are DEFAULT/SEED values — the administrator must be able to edit every figure; nothing may be hardcoded in code.
1. Individual — covers 1 user — Annual Platform Fee: RM60.
2. Family — covers up to 5 users — Annual Platform Fee: RM240.
3. Business — covers up to 20 users — Annual Platform Fee: RM720.
4. Business Plus — covers 21 up to 100 users — Annual Platform Fee: RM3,000.
5. Enterprise — covers approximately 101–1,000 users — user limit configurable by administrator — Annual Platform Fee: Custom quotation (no fixed default).

6. Community — designed for associations, NGOs, clubs, community organisations, or larger groups — can support more than 1,000 users — user limit configurable by administrator — Annual Platform Fee: Custom quotation (no fixed default). NOTE (Claude’s observation, not yet confirmed with Chris): this “Community” category appears to be how a CBE organization itself would subscribe under the GLADE Public Model — its relationship to the EXISTING group_labels.subscription_tier FREE/PAID enum (Section 51) has NOT been clarified or assumed; needs an explicit follow-up question before any schema work merges or replaces either concept.

- Vendor Rebate Rule: all users under all six categories receive the SAME vendor rebate percentage according to whatever rebate each vendor campaign offers (e.g. a vendor offering 10% rebate gives all eligible users 10%, regardless of category). The category does NOT change, reduce, or increase a vendor’s rebate percentage. There is NO upline, downline, recruitment commission, team commission, group commission, or multi-tier rebate structure anywhere in the Public Model — the six categories exist ONLY to determine how many users are covered by the Annual Platform Fee.

- Administrator must be able to configure, per category: maximum users allowed, Annual Platform Fee amount, and whether that category is available for individual/family/business/enterprise/community use.

57. GLADE Vendor Referral Incentive Scheme (27 Aug 2026) — NEW BUSINESS MODEL, DICTATED VERBATIM BY CHRIS, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED

- Dictated by Chris in full immediately after Section 56, same instruction to write to master spec now. This is a SEPARATE scheme from the GLADE Public Model membership categories above — it governs how a Vendor Referral (an existing platform role: Affiliate/Team Leader/Group Leader/other approved Partner role) is rewarded for bringing a new Vendor onto the platform.

- 1. VENDOR FEES: Annual Hosting Fee RM1,200/year. Registration & Activation Fee RM300, one-time only, charged only when the Vendor first joins and is activated. From Year 2 onward the Vendor pays only the RM1,200 Annual Hosting Fee.

- 2. VENDOR REFERRAL INCENTIVE: if a Vendor is referred by a registered Vendor Referral, the RM300 Registration & Activation Fee is allocated as RM100 to General Link, RM100 to the Referral for Stage 1, RM100 to the Referral for Stage 2. Maximum Referral Incentive = RM200 total to the Referral; General Link retains RM100. The RM200 is a ONE-TIME incentive only — NOT a permanent commission and NOT an ongoing percentage of the Vendor’s future sales.
- 3. STAGE 1 — ACTIVATION INCENTIVE (RM100): paid when Vendor registration is completed AND the RM300 Registration & Activation Fee is paid AND the Vendor is successfully activated.

- 4. STAGE 2 — 90-DAY ACTIVITY INCENTIVE (RM100): paid only when the Vendor becomes genuinely active within 90 days of activation. Example qualifying condition: at least 1 valid transaction OR at least 1 valid Rebate Claim — the exact qualifying condition must be configurable by Admin. If the Vendor does not meet the qualifying condition within 90 days, the second RM100 is NOT payable.

- 5. NO PERMANENT VENDOR SALES COMMISSION: the Referral never receives an ongoing percentage of the Vendor’s sales. Once the maximum RM200 has been paid, the Vendor Referral Incentive ends permanently for that Vendor — this protects General Link from creating an unlimited future payment obligation.

- 6. SEPARATE AFFILIATE / TEAM LEADER / GROUP LEADER EARNINGS: a Vendor Referral may also hold other roles (Affiliate, Team Leader, Group Leader, other approved Partner roles). These are handled COMPLETELY SEPARATELY from the Vendor Referral Incentive. If consumers later purchase from the Vendor through the Referral’s own team/affiliate/group structure, that person may earn according to the EXISTING General Link Rebate & Earning Distribution Scheme — that earning is separate from, and unrelated to, the one-time RM200 Vendor Referral Incentive.

- 7. SYSTEM TRACKING: the system must record, per referred Vendor — Vendor ID, Vendor Referral ID, Registration Date, Activation Date, RM300 Payment Status, Stage 1 RM100 Status, 90-Day Qualification Period (window), Qualifying Transaction / Rebate Claim (what satisfied it), Stage 2 RM100 Status, Total Incentive Paid, Payment Date, and an overall Status: Pending / Qualified / Paid / Expired / Cancelled.

69. Session Update — Accounting Engine Decision: Self-Hosted ERPNext via API, Not a Composer Package (28 Aug 2026)

- Chris asked where the AR Module is, pointed out the Financial Accounting Module only has AP + GL built (no formal Accounts Receivable, Inventory, Fixed Asset Register, Cash Book, or Bank Reconciliation), and referenced his original written brief: integrate a free, open-source accounting system via API (Akaunting Community Edition preferred, ERPNext or Odoo Community Edition as fallbacks) so GLADE stays independent of and able to swap out the accounting backend. That brief had not actually been evaluated in the earlier accounting-integration report (see Tasks #138-139, 28 Aug 2026), which covered QuickBooks/Xero/Sage/AutoCount/SQL Account/Million instead — a real gap, corrected this session.

- First proposed, in error, an in-process Laravel Composer package (centrex/laravel-accounting) — Chris corrected this immediately, since a package embedded in GLADE's own code does not meet his API-based, independent, swappable requirement from the original brief.

- Properly evaluated the three systems Chris actually specified. Akaunting Community Edition: BSL license (only converts to GPL 4 years after each release), and self-hosted installs still require a mandatory API key that phones home to Akaunting's own servers to validate plan/feature access — conflicts with "platform remains independent." Odoo Community Edition: the full Accounting app is Enterprise-only; Community's unlocked "Full Accounting" is missing standard reports and bank-sync integrations, likely failing several of Chris's required reports. ERPNext: MIT licensed, no gating, no phone-home dependency, full Accounting + Inventory + Assets modules included free, native documented REST API, actively maintained (v16 shipped January 2026).

- Decision: adopt ERPNext, self-hosted, connected to GLADE over its REST API. Finance staff will use ERPNext's own web interface directly for day-to-day AR/AP/GL/Inventory/Asset/Bank-Reconciliation data entry, reusing its mature UI rather than rebuilding every screen in Blade; GLADE's own Finance Dashboard will pull summary figures (Trial Balance, P&L, Balance Sheet, AR/AP Aging) back in via API for the KPI boxes already built.

80. Session Update — Master + Add-On Chart of Accounts, Monthly-Band Document Numbering, Document Number Control, Full Purchase Order Module (3-4 Sep 2026)

Chris asked directly whether the chart of accounts differs across temples/branches/states, and proposed the design himself: “i suggest the default is from one master chart of account, how ever if temple A and B is different i dont think every gl code is different , may be you can add the 'add on' chart of account seperately for individual temple or branch or state.” This exact design was built: cbe_chart_of_accounts gained a nullable cbe_node_id column. NULL means a shared master account visible to the whole federation, editable only by the community's root/HQ node. A specific node ID means a local "add-on" account visible and editable only by that one temple/branch/state. Account-code uniqueness is enforced at the application level (not a database unique index), because a nullable column in a MySQL unique index treats every NULL as a distinct value and would not correctly enforce uniqueness among shared accounts.

During this build, a related gap was self-caught and fixed: bank account and petty cash fund GL accounts (auto-created when a new bank account or petty cash fund is set up) were still being created as shared accounts. Fixed so these are always scoped to their owning node regardless of that node's root status, since a specific bank account or petty cash fund belongs to exactly one entity. A further sweep of every chart-of-accounts query in the system (Cash Flow Statement, Chart of Accounts Enquiry, General Ledger Enquiry, Account Balance Report, and income/expense category mapping) caught and fixed several places that would otherwise have leaked one node's local add-on accounts into another node's screens, or hidden a node's own bank accounts from its own Cash Flow Statement.

Chris then asked whether debtor/creditor records and every document number (JV, PV, PR, Pledge, Receipt, Invoice, PCV, PCT, debit note, credit note, PO) are fully separate per entity, using the example that Company A can be a customer of Temple A but a supplier to Temple B. Confirmed yes for all existing document types — every one is scoped by cbe_node_id — but two real gaps were disclosed rather than assumed away: Debit and Credit Notes had no formatted document number (only an internal system ID), and no Purchase Order feature existed anywhere in the system.

Chris confirmed both gaps should be closed and gave a specific numbering design: “a document number must have it owns. by right you should have one master file keep track the starting number, the user can reset base on periodically basis, example January month is from 01000-01999 february is 02000-02999 december will be 12001-12999.” Document numbering was redesigned from a continuous yearly counter (PREFIX-YYYY-MM-NNNN) to a fixed monthly band embedded directly in the number (PREFIX-YYYY-MMSSS): January = 01000-01999, February = 02000-02999, through December = 12000-12999, resetting to the start of a new band every month, per node, per document type.

A new Document Number Control master file screen was built (Master File Maintenance, Admin-only) showing every document type's current band, last number used, and next number to be issued, for any month/year. An authorised user can reset the starting number for a period — required for Chris's own stated use case of periodic resets — but every reset is written to a permanent audit log (old number, new number, reason, who reset it, when) rather than silently overwriting the counter, and resetting a number backward into already-issued territory requires an explicit on-screen acknowledgement that this may create a duplicate number. This audit control was added using standard internal-control practice, per Chris's instruction not to be asked accounting-design questions.

Debit Notes, AP Debit Notes, AR Debit Notes and AR Credit Notes each now generate their own formatted document number (DN, APDN, ARDN, ARCN respectively) under the same monthly-band scheme, shown as a new Doc No. column on each listing screen.

A full Purchase Order module was built, completing the standard 3-stage procurement chain used during temple events and festival prayer seasons: Purchase Request (internal ask, already existed) → Purchase Order (commitment sent to the supplier, new) → Purchase Bill (what was actually billed, already existed). A Purchase Order does not post to the General Ledger — placing an order is not yet a liability under accrual accounting, only the resulting Bill is — this accounting treatment was decided directly, not asked. A Purchase Order can be created two ways: a one-click conversion from an already-approved Purchase Request, or a standalone new Purchase Order for orders with no prior internal request, covering ad-hoc festival purchases. Each Purchase Order carries its own PO number under the same monthly-band scheme, tracks status (Open, Partially Received, Fully Received, Closed, Cancelled), and converts into a real Purchase Bill when the supplier's invoice arrives, which automatically closes the Order. A new PO Outstanding report shows ordered vs. billed-so-far vs. outstanding amount for every open order.

Every change in this arc was verified directly against the live code before being marked complete: all touched migrations, the accounting service, the accounting controller, the finance controller, routes, all new and modified screens, and all 3 language files were brace/syntax balance-checked; every new route was traced to its controller method and confirmed correctly ordered (create-route registered ahead of the wildcard show-route); language keys were confirmed to resolve with zero duplicates and full parity across English, Malay and Chinese.

Database migrations: 4 new migrations were created this session and have not yet been run against the live database — add_node_id_to_chart_of_accounts, add_month_band_to_document_sequences, add_doc_ref_no_to_notes, and create_cbe_purchase_orders. Chris still needs to run php artisan migrate.

82. Session Update — Purchasing Management Module Phase 2 Complete: Goods/Service Receipt, Purchase Return, Supplier Invoice 3-Way Matching, Budget & Purchase Commitment, Full Reports Suite (4 Sep 2026, Task #394, Phase 2)

Completed Phase 2 of the Purchasing Management module (queued at the end of item #81/Phase 1), closing out every remaining piece of Chris’s original written specification: Goods/Service Receipt, Purchase Return, Supplier Invoice 3-way matching, Budget & Purchase Commitment, and the full Purchasing reports suite.

Goods/Service Receipt (GRN): records what was actually received against a Purchase Order — goods delivery or service completion, one shared table with a type flag since both follow the identical receive-against-PO workflow. Supports partial receipt (a PO can have several GRNs over time), tracks received/rejected quantity and a condition note (Good/Damaged/Short) per line, and keeps a running cumulative received-quantity total on each PO line so the PO’s own status (Open / Partially Received / Fully Received) updates automatically without re-summing every GRN each time. Cancelling a GRN reverses that running total and recomputes the PO status.

Purchase Return: goods returned to a supplier, always entered against an existing GRN (not directly against a PO), with its own reason and status lifecycle (Draft / Confirmed / Credit Raised / Cancelled). Raising a Debit Note from a Purchase Return pre-fills the supplier, amount (summed from the return’s lines) and reason, and writes the link back onto the return (status moves to Credit Raised, with the Debit Note’s reference stored) so the two documents stay traceable to each other — completing the drill-down chain the spec asked for (GL Journal → Debit Note → Purchase Return → GRN → PO).

Supplier Invoice 3-way matching: a Supplier Invoice can now be created directly from a confirmed GRN, showing the GRN’s received quantity and the PO’s unit price as read-only reference columns alongside editable invoiced quantity/price fields. On save, the invoiced amounts are compared against the PO (price) and the GRN (quantity) with a small tolerance, and the bill is tagged with a match status — Matched, Price Variance, Quantity Variance, No PO, or No GRN — shown as a badge on the Bill Enquiry screen. The GRN is marked Posted once billed, which doubles as duplicate-billing control at the source-document level (the same GRN cannot be invoiced twice). A second, simpler duplicate-invoice-number check was also added to the existing quick PO-to-Bill conversion path: the same supplier cannot have two bills recorded under the same invoice number (a friendly on-screen check backed by a database unique index).

Budget & Purchase Commitment: a lighter-weight design than the spec’s full budget-versioning example, decided directly per Chris’s standing instruction not to be asked accounting-design questions — one budget line per node/fiscal year, optionally scoped to a Department/Project and/or Fund (left blank for an all-scope budget). A Budget Utilisation report (kept on-screen with Prev/Next year navigation, rather than an Excel download, since it is meant to be checked routinely rather than filed) shows, per budget line: the budget amount, PO Commitment (approved POs not yet closed or cancelled), Actual Invoice (non-cancelled bills), Actual Payment, Remaining, and Utilisation %. Commitment and Actual Invoice never double-count the same spend, because a PO automatically moves to Closed status once it has been fully billed.

Purchasing Reports: a new Purchasing Reports Hub groups 7 new downloadable Excel reports — Purchase Requisition Listing, Cancelled Purchase Orders, Purchase Return Listing, PO/GRN/Invoice Matching Variance, Unbilled Goods/Service Received, Pending Approval Listing (Purchase Requisitions and Purchase Orders awaiting approval in one sheet), and Purchase by Department/Fund (a single report with a Group By selector, rather than two near-identical reports) — plus links out to the existing PO Outstanding report, the on-screen Budget Utilisation report, and the Expense-by-Supplier/Expense-by-Category reports already built in the AP Reports Hub (not duplicated here). The main Purchasing hub screen was tidied to match: PO Outstanding and Budget Utilisation moved into the new Reports Hub, and a single "Purchasing Reports" tile added, keeping the transactional hub focused on the day-to-day procurement chain (Suppliers → Requisition → Quotation → Order → Bill → Goods Receipt → Return → Budget) the same way AP and AR already separate their own transactional hub from their Reports Hub.

83. Session Update — Purchasing Module Gap-Closure: Drill-Down Links, Supplier Procurement History, Capital Asset Purchase Flow, GL Posting Control Status Trail, Purchasing Audit Trail (4 Sep 2026, Task #394 gap-fix)

Chris asked directly, after the Phase 2 completion message: “have you done evrything i want in purchasing Module?” Rather than reflexively confirming, the live code was re-checked against Chris's original written 31-section specification section by section — Supplier Enquiry, Drill-Down, GL Integration/Posting Control, Capital Asset Purchase flow and Audit Trail in particular. This surfaced 5 real gaps, which were disclosed honestly (“So: not everything, no.”) before any further work was done. Chris replied: “complete everything dont leave any gap.” This item records the full closure of all 5 gaps.

Gap 1 — Drill-down links: several purchasing screens referenced a source or destination document by number only, with no way to click through. Purchase Order now links back to its originating Purchase Request and forward to every Bill raised against it; Goods Receipt links back to its Purchase Order; Purchase Return links to both its Goods Receipt and Purchase Order (this also caught and fixed a pre-existing label bug — the Purchase Return screen was showing the GRN reference number under an “Against Purchase Order” label, a real copy/paste mismatch from an earlier session); Bill Enquiry now links to its Purchase Order and Goods Receipt; every supplier name shown across these screens now links to Supplier Enquiry. A brand-new Purchase Request detail screen was also built, since requisitions previously had no dedicated show page at all — the requisition listing now links into it.

Gap 2 — Supplier Procurement History: Supplier Enquiry only ever showed the Accounts Payable side of a supplier (bills, payments, notes), with no view of the purchasing side (requisitions, quotations, orders, receipts, returns). A new Supplier Procurement History screen was built, combining all five document types for one supplier into a single date-ordered activity list with a status column and a drill-down link on every row, reached via a new “Purchasing Activity” button on Supplier Enquiry.

Gap 3 — Capital Asset Purchase flow: the spec asks for a Purchasing → Invoice → AP → Fixed Asset → GL flow when a purchase is for a capital item rather than an expense. Tracing through how this system actually posts to the General Ledger mattered here: a Bill already posts its journal entry (Dr the category's mapped GL account / Cr Accounts Payable) the instant it is created, so if a Bill's line is coded to a Fixed Asset account, the balance sheet is already correctly capitalised at that moment. The new “Create Fixed Asset” action on Bill Enquiry therefore only creates the depreciation-tracking register entry, carrying across the cost, date and the Bill's own already-posted journal reference — it deliberately does not post a second journal entry, which would have double-counted the asset. While designing this, a genuine pre-existing bug was self-caught and fixed: the asset-capitalisation posting method has checked a journal_id column on the fixed asset table as a duplicate-posting guard since an earlier session, but that column was never actually added to the table — meaning the guard silently did nothing the whole time. This is fixed by a new migration adding the missing journal_id, gl_posting_status and bill_id columns, and by wiring the guard's own update call that had been missing.

Gap 4 — GL Posting Control status trail: the spec describes named posting-control stages (Ready for AP, AP Invoice Created, GL Posted, plus Error/Reversed states). This system's GL posting is synchronous, not a staged queue — there is no batch or async posting step anywhere — so rather than fabricating workflow states that do not really exist, a computed status (worked out fresh each time the Purchase Order screen is opened, not stored in the database) honestly maps the PO's real approval/status data and its linked Bills' real posting status onto the closest matching named stage. Purchase Order now shows a horizontal step tracker (Ready for AP → AP Invoice Created → GL Posted) with a separate alert badge for any error or reversal state, alongside the existing Pending Approval / Rejected / Cancelled badges.

Gap 5 — Purchasing Audit Trail: previously every purchasing document only ever showed its latest action (a single created_by / approved_by column each) with no history of everything that happened to it, and nowhere to see activity across the whole module at once. A new append-only event log table, cbe_purchasing_audit_log, now records one row per action (Created, Approved, Rejected, Converted, Cancelled, Received, Matched, Supplier Selected, Quote Saved) across every purchasing document type — Purchase Request, Quotation, Purchase Order, Goods Receipt, Purchase Return and the 3-way-matched Bill — written alongside, never instead of, each document's own status columns, and never updated or deleted afterwards. A new Purchasing Audit Trail screen browses this log, filterable by document type, with every row's document number linking straight back to that document's own show screen; it is reached from a new tile on the Purchasing Reports Hub. Two more missing-variable bugs were self-caught and fixed while wiring this logging in: the convert-Requisition-to-Purchase-Order and convert-Purchase-Order-to-Bill actions both ran an existence-check query whose result was never assigned to a variable, so there was no document reference available to log — both now capture that result properly.

Every change in this arc was verified directly against the live code before being marked complete: every touched PHP file (the accounting controller, the accounting service, both new migrations) was balance-checked for matching braces/brackets/parentheses/quotes after every edit; every English/Malay/Chinese language file was checked for exact 3-way key parity and zero duplicates (1,126 keys, fully matched, confirmed both by direct key-set comparison and by cross-referencing every literal language-key call across all Purchasing Blade views against the key list); every one of the 288 routes in the Purchasing/Accounting route group was traced to a real controller method that exists; and every one of the 126 distinct views referenced by the controller was confirmed to exist on disk.

Chris asked to build out the Fixed Asset Module and pasted a complete, extremely detailed 30-section written specification (Master File/Setup, Asset Entry/Transaction, Enquiry, Reports, Depreciation, Asset Disposal, Asset Transfer, GL Integration, Reconciliation, Period Control, Audit Trail, Security and Approval), explicitly confirming MYR/RM as the sole base currency with no multi-currency requirement. After the module was built and Chris said “all Fixed asset completed 100% as per my requirement”, this was checked rather than reflexively confirmed — Phase 3 (Enquiry + Reports) and Phase 4 (Reconciliation/GL drill-down/Audit Trail/Security) were still outstanding against the written spec, and this was disclosed honestly before any further work was claimed done. Chris replied “yes do ALL and complete 100%”. This item records the full build across all four phases.

Phase 1 — Asset Category and Asset Location master files were added (cbe_asset_categories, cbe_asset_locations), each admin-configurable and lazily seeded the same way the Chart of Accounts is, never hardcoded business data. Asset Category carries three GL account mapping columns (Fixed Asset / Accumulated Depreciation / Depreciation Expense) with a resolveAssetGlAccount() fallback so any asset without a category keeps using the single global default account exactly as before — zero behaviour change for pre-upgrade assets. Department reuses the existing Cost Centre master’s DEPARTMENT type rather than a new table, matching the convention already established in Purchasing. Reducing Balance depreciation was added alongside Straight Line, implemented as double-declining balance (2 / useful-life-months applied to current Net Book Value) and capped to land exactly on the depreciable ceiling on the final posting — disclosed as a simplification since true reducing-balance mathematically never reaches the salvage value exactly. The asset detail screen was redesigned into a fixed-height, no-scroll, Prev/Next-only multi-page flow (per the standing UI rule) rather than a single scrolling page.

Phase 2 — Asset Improvement (Additional Cost) posts its own GL entry (Dr Fixed Asset, Cr Cash) without ever overwriting the asset’s Original Cost; a computed Revised Cost (Original + all posted Improvements) is used everywhere that matters — depreciation, disposal, Net Book Value — preserving a clean audit trail of what was originally paid. Asset Transfer updates the same asset row (location/department/fund) rather than creating a new record, since the spec explicitly says an asset must never be duplicated on transfer; no GL entry is posted since moving an asset is not a monetary event, and a full from/to history is logged. Disposal and Write-Off were unified onto one flow with a disposal_type field (Sale/Donation/Scrap/Write-Off/Loss/Other) plus a new Asset Condition field and a supporting-document upload, rather than building a separate Write-Off module. A generic Maker-Checker approval workflow was added for all four gated actions (Acquisition/Disposal/Transfer/Improvement), reusing the exact same per-node approval-threshold infrastructure already built for Bill Payments and Bank Transfers, through one new staging table (cbe_fixed_asset_requests) and plugged into the existing Pending Approvals screen — disposal approval is gated on whichever is larger of cash proceeds or Net Book Value (so a zero-proceeds write-off of a valuable asset still requires approval), and transfer approval is gated purely on whether Maker-Checker is switched on for the node, since a transfer has no natural monetary amount to compare against a threshold. The asset detail screen gained a third page — Asset History — combining Improvements and Transfers into one chronological trail per spec section 16.

Phase 3 — A new Asset Enquiry screen lets a treasurer search every fixed asset by keyword (name or tag), category, location, department, fund, status or supplier, mirroring the same search-then-list pattern already used elsewhere in the app. The existing Fixed Asset Schedule report was upgraded into the full Asset Register the spec describes, adding Category, Location, Department, Fund, Supplier and an Original / Additional / Revised Cost breakdown rather than a single Cost column. Six new downloadable reports were built: Asset Acquisition Report, Asset Transfer Report, Asset Write-Off Report (Asset Condition and Supporting Document included), and Asset by Location / by Department / by Fund reports (each grouped with a subtotal per group and a grand total). A new Fixed Asset Reports Hub page consolidates every one of these alongside the pre-existing Disposal Listing, Depreciation Listing and FA/GL Reconciliation reports, reached from the sidebar and from the Fixed Assets list header.

Phase 4 — Two real accuracy bugs were self-caught and fixed while building this phase, both introduced by the Phase 2 Improvement feature: the FA/GL Reconciliation report compared the sub-ledger’s Net Book Value against the GL control account balance using only the original acquisition_cost, silently ignoring that a posted Improvement debits the same Fixed Asset GL account — this understated the sub-ledger side and would have shown a false difference for any asset that ever received an Improvement; the Disposal Listing report had the identical bug in its Gain/Loss column. Both now read the same computed Revised Cost the disposal and reconciliation logic itself actually uses. GL drill-down was extended per spec section 10: each depreciation entry on the asset detail screen now links to its own journal, the disposal information line links to the disposal’s journal (looked up by source_type/source_id, since disposeFixedAsset() posts a journal without writing it back onto the asset’s own journal_id column — that column already means “the capitalisation journal” everywhere else it is read), and each Improvement row on the new History page links to its journal. A Fixed Asset Audit Trail was built as an append-only event log (cbe_fixed_asset_audit_log), an exact mirror of the existing Purchasing Audit Trail pattern, recording one row per action — Created, Submitted for Approval, Approved, Rejected, Edited, Depreciation Posted, Improvement Posted, Transferred, Disposed — across every fixed asset action, written alongside, never instead of, the asset’s own status columns, with its own browsable screen linking back to each asset.

Security and Approval (spec sections 27–28) required disclosure rather than new construction: this application has no granular per-action permission engine anywhere in the codebase — the entire security model, in every module including Purchasing, AR and AP, is one single role check (accounting-admin, i.e. role === ADMIN) used only to exempt an Admin from the Maker-Checker self-approval block, plus the Maker-Checker approval threshold itself. Building a genuine 12-permission access-control matrix (View/Create/Edit/Approve Asset, Process Depreciation, Transfer/Dispose/Write Off Asset, Import to GL, Reverse Transaction, View Reports, Maintain Asset Setup, Maintain GL Mapping) with real enforcement would mean a new roles-and-permissions subsystem touching every route in the app, not a Fixed Asset Module feature — and a permissions table that existed but enforced nothing would be actively misleading. This was disclosed to Chris directly rather than silently built as a decorative, non-functional screen; the existing Maker-Checker gate on Acquisition/Disposal/Transfer/Improvement already provides the real dual-control the spec is asking for in practice.

Every change across all four phases was verified directly against the live code, the same way as every previous gap-closure arc: every touched PHP file (the accounting controller, the accounting service, five new migrations, routes/web.php) was balance-checked for matching braces/brackets/parentheses/quotes after every edit; every English/Malay/Chinese language file was checked for exact 3-way key parity and zero duplicates (1,223 keys, fully matched); every new route was traced to a real controller method that exists, and every view referenced by those methods was confirmed to exist on disk.

Database migrations: 1 new migration was created this session and has not yet been run against the live database — create_fixed_asset_audit_log_table (creates the new cbe_fixed_asset_audit_log append-only event log table). The 2 migrations from the Phase 2 session (create_fixed_asset_requests_table, create_asset_improvements_and_transfers) were already run by Chris earlier in this arc.

Phase 1 (Upload + Extraction) built PdfStatementExtractionService, which reads digital-text bank statement PDFs — no OCR, so scanned/photographed statements are explicitly rejected rather than guessed at — and stages every identifiable transaction line for review; nothing posts to the books until Chris checks and commits. New tables: cbe_ai_statement_batches, cbe_ai_statement_documents, cbe_ai_extracted_transactions.

Phase 2 (Rule-Based Classification) added TransactionClassificationService, which classifies each line into one of ten categories (Supplier, Customer, Donation, Membership, Asset, Transfer, Bank Charge, Loan, Adjustment, Other) using either a learned rule (cbe_ai_classification_rules, reinforced every time Chris confirms or corrects a category) or one of eight built-in generic keyword rules; no confident match leaves the category null rather than guessing. The same pass pairs same-amount credit/debit lines within a statement as a possible restricted/designated fund — the RM50,000 donation-in/disbursement-out pattern Chris flagged from his friend's FTAM Klang reference file — and flags it for his confirmation instead of silently blending it into ordinary income or expense.

Phase 3 (Draft Master Creation) added PartyMatchingService, which suggests a supplier/customer/donor name from the transaction description using only real signal, never a fabricated guess, matches it to an existing master record by exact name, or creates a new one flagged is_draft = true for Chris to confirm or correct — never done silently before he has seen and can edit it.

Phase 4 (GL Posting Engine) added new orchestration methods directly on the existing CbeAccountingService, not a parallel service, so they could reuse its private posting helpers: AI-classified bank transactions post through the same postJournal() every other module uses, for categories that need no subledger (Bank Charge, Donation, Membership, Adjustment, Other) and only when confidence clears the auto-post threshold. Supplier, Customer and Asset categories were deliberately excluded here to avoid double-posting once Phases 5 and 6 handled them properly.

Phase 5 (AP/AR Posting) added allocateAiPaymentToBillOrInvoice(), which matches a Supplier/Customer payment against a real, already-open bill or invoice for that exact party and amount, and posts through the existing postBillPayment()/postInvoicePayment() — including the same maker-checker approval gate bill payments already have. This is deliberately conservative: most of Chris's direct-cheque payments will not have a pre-recorded bill to match, which was disclosed to him as expected behaviour, not a bug.

Phase 6 (Fixed Asset Intelligence) matches a detected asset purchase against the app's real twelve seeded asset categories (Land, Buildings, Renovation, Furniture & Fittings, Office Equipment, Computer Equipment, Audio Visual Equipment, Electrical Equipment, Vehicles, Religious Equipment, Kitchen Equipment, Other Fixed Assets) by keyword, capitalises it via the existing createFixedAssetDirect(), and treats the vendor as an ordinary cbe_suppliers record rather than a new master table.

Phase 7 (Multi-Year Continuity) added StatementContinuityService, which checks a newly uploaded statement's opening balance against what the GL says it should be — computed purely from the bank account's real opening balance plus everything posted since, never invented — and flags a mismatch over RM1 or a gap of three days or more since the last statement uploaded for that account. Chris explicitly scoped this phase to continuity checks only, via a direct clarifying question, deferring a general accrual/prepayment/suspense-account checklist as separate future work since it risked overlapping the existing Year-End Closing feature.

Phase 8 (Learning Engine + Exception Centre) added a Learned Rules screen showing and letting Chris deactivate any rule the system has learned, alongside a per-node configurable auto-post confidence threshold (cbe_ai_automation_settings, replacing a hardcoded 60 used throughout Phases 4–6), and a new Exception Management Centre screen grouping every outstanding item — unclassified, low confidence, restricted fund, draft masters, continuity, unmatched AP/AR — by type with counts, rather than one-by-one prompts, per Chris's own "temporary ledger, row by row" request.

Phase 9 (Complete Audit Trail) added cbe_ai_audit_log, mirroring the existing Purchasing/Fixed Asset/Bank Reconciliation audit log pattern exactly: it records every upload, parse (success or failure), continuity flag, commit — with the full reasoning behind it (category, classification source, confidence, party match, posting outcome) — rejection, duplicate skip, and threshold/rule change. Anything the AI could not confidently resolve is written to the log as "Unverified," never guessed.

Phase 10 (Reporting Tie-In) confirmed that AI-posted transactions already flow correctly into Trial Balance, Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow, since they post through the same GL tables as every manual entry, and found and fixed the one place that did not: the Annual Report Pack's Income & Expenditure tab was calculating from a legacy table instead of the same GL-based helper the standalone Profit & Loss report already used, meaning AI-sourced entries would have been silently missing from that one export only. Also confirmed no "Form 9" mislabeling exists anywhere in the ROS module (that term correctly appears only in the unrelated Vendor/SSM document checklist) and that the restricted-fund flagging built in Phase 2 already routes to the Phase 8 Exception Centre — both were already correct, nothing to fix. Matching the Annual Report Pack's exact layout to the live eROSES Penyata Tahunan portal format is deferred to a separate future task pending screenshots from Chris.

Phase 11 (Final Verification) confirmed the AI Accounting Automation sidebar section sits immediately after Bank Reconciliation as instructed; balance-checked every PHP file in the module — the controller, five services, and nine migrations — for matching braces, brackets and parentheses; traced all 13 AI module routes to a real controller method and, where applicable, a real existing view (seven Blade views, all using the same fixed-height no-scroll container and Prev/Next-only pagination as every other screen in the app); and confirmed the English/Malay/Chinese cbe_ai.php language file has exact three-way key parity with zero duplicates across all 144 keys.

STATUS: The AI-Powered Accounting Automation Management Module (Task #397) is now complete end-to-end across all 11 phases, sharing one GL posting engine and one GL-based reporting engine with the rest of the application rather than any parallel logic. Disclosed limitations carried forward rather than fabricated: AP/AR auto-matching only helps when a bill or invoice is already recorded; posting_note/flag_note store translated text rather than a stable code, a theoretical locale-switch fragility consistent with the pre-existing pattern elsewhere in the app; and the Annual Report Pack's exact layout has not yet been matched to the live eROSES portal, pending screenshots from Chris. All 9 migrations (Phases 1–9) have been run and confirmed by Chris; Phases 10 and 11 required no new migration.

Chris pushed back on a first proposal to keep religious-practice accounts unchanged while only renaming generic labels, worried that any leftover "Temple" wording anywhere could make an unrelated future user (his own example: a Chinese Chamber of Commerce) feel they were using a temple-only system. Verified via direct code research that this concern does not apply to his own data: CBE is architecturally multi-tenant, each organization isolated by group_label_id with its own independent Chart of Accounts, and a brand-new organization is seeded with a small generic starter set (about 13 accounts) rather than any copy of another organization's accounts. Agreed a renaming approach on that basis: generic/structural labels — "General Temple Fund", "Temple Buildings", "Temple Maintenance", "Temple Cleaning", "Temple Petty Cash", and "Building Fund" wording that literally read "build-temple" in the Chinese — became "Entity"/"机构" (the same Chinese word the app already uses elsewhere for "your organization"), while genuine religious-practice accounts (Incense, Candle, Joss Paper, Lamp Offering, Priest/Monk Fees, Ancestral Tablet, Ceremony) were kept exactly as given, since they describe what this specific organization actually does, not the system.

On review, proactively recommended three content additions, all confirmed by Chris: a "Membership Fee Income" account (4050) — since the AI Accounting Automation module already classifies transactions into a MEMBERSHIP category with nowhere in this file for it to post — and "Grant Income" (4940) and "Investment Income" (4950) under Other Income.

Built a one-off, idempotent Artisan command (php artisan cbe:import-coa --group=<id>, app/Console/Commands/ImportStarterChartOfAccounts.php) rather than a permanent upload screen, per Chris's choice of a quick one-time import over a reusable feature. The command inserts parent/summary accounts first, then child/detail accounts linked via parent_account_id, skips any account code already present for that community on re-run, and requires an explicit --group= whenever more than one CBE community exists rather than guessing — which is exactly what happened live: running the command surfaced the pre-existing "Rotary Club Uptown" test community alongside Chris's own, directly confirming the isolation design in practice rather than just in theory.
Chris ran the command against 马来西亚道教总会 (group_label_id 47159e62-7056-4ede-be21-074315c7be30): 232 accounts inserted, 0 skipped, confirmed successful.

88. Session Update — AI Module Phase 17: Printable PDF Official Receipts, Composer Package Install + Windows Permissions Fix (10 Sep 2026, Task #397 follow-up)

Chris authorized Phase 17 (the final phase of the six-phase Task #397 follow-up arc, Phases 12–17) to add printable, downloadable PDF Official Receipts, since NGO practice requires a physical receipt for every donor. Built app/Services/NumberToWordsService.php, a small self-contained Ringgit amount-to-words converter (“Ringgit Malaysia Five Hundred Only” style, matching standard Malaysian cheque/receipt wording) needing no external package. Added AdminCbeReceiptController::downloadPdf(), reusing the exact same receipt lookup query as the existing show() method so the PDF always matches the on-screen receipt. Created a new Blade template, resources/views/admin/cbe-kpi/receipts/pdf.blade.php, built with tables and block elements only — the existing browser-print receipt view uses flexbox, which the dompdf PDF renderer does not support, so the two views intentionally do not share CSS, only the app's one standard font and colour scheme (blue #1565C0). Added a new route (cbe-kpi/receipts/pdf) and a “Download PDF” button next to the existing “Print Receipt” button on the receipt screen. Also wired the Phase 14 AI-driven donation receipt display (show-document.blade.php) to link through to this same receipt page: added a leftJoin on cbe_receipts (matched on cbe_node_id + receipt_no) to AiAccountingController::showDocument() so a receipt number shown on an AI-processed bank statement line is now a clickable link, not just plain text.

New language keys (btn_download_receipt_pdf, receipt_amount_words_label, receipt_received_by_label, receipt_authorized_signature_label) added to lang/en, lang/ms and lang/zh admin_cbe_directory.php — verified exact 253-key parity across all three locales with zero duplicates, and every admin_cbe_directory.* key referenced in the two receipt views cross-checked against defined keys with none missing. Balance-checked all touched PHP files (NumberToWordsService.php, AdminCbeReceiptController.php, AiAccountingController.php) for matching brackets/braces/parentheses, and confirmed matching @if/@endif, @foreach/@endforeach, @forelse/@empty/@endforelse and @php/@endphp counts on all three touched Blade views.

The one composer package this phase needed (barryvdh/laravel-dompdf) hit a real installation snag worth recording: after composer require completed, Laravel's post-install package:discover step failed with “The bootstrap\cache directory must be present and writable,” even though the folder existed. Traced this to a Windows Read-only attribute stuck on the entire generallink folder tree (visible via attrib, showing R on generallink and everything under it, while the parent xampp folder itself showed no flag) — PHP's is_writable() check on Windows reads this attribute directly rather than the real NTFS security permissions (which were already correct, confirmed via icacls showing Everyone:Full Control). Google Drive Desktop, which auto-backs up this folder per Chris's setup, was suspected first and ruled out by ending its process, which did not clear the flag. The fix required an elevated (Run as Administrator) Command Prompt running attrib -r “bootstrap\cache” /s /d — a normal, non-elevated attrib -r silently failed to clear it. Once cleared, php artisan package:discover --ansi completed successfully, registering barryvdh/laravel-dompdf alongside all 14 other already-installed packages.

STATUS: All Phase 17 code is written and verified as above, but Chris ended the session here (“continue tomorrow”) immediately after confirming package:discover succeeded — the actual “Download PDF” button has not yet been clicked and tested end-to-end in the browser, so the rendered PDF's layout and correctness are not yet confirmed. This is the one remaining step before Task #397's full 17-phase arc (Phases 1–17) can be marked complete. Next step on return: test the Download PDF button on a real receipt, confirm the PDF opens and reads correctly (organization name, receipt number, date, payer, description, amount in figures and words, issued-by, signature line), then close out Phase 17 and the whole AI-Powered Accounting Automation Management Module.
